#### Smaller local units

- **Uttar Pradesh** — 1 biswa = 1,350 sq ft; 1 biswansi = 67.5 sq ft.
- **Bihar** — 1 katha = 1,361 sq ft; 1 dhur = 68.05 sq ft.
- **West Bengal** — 1 katha = 720 sq ft; 1 chatak = 45 sq ft.
- **Assam** — 1 katha = 2,880 sq ft; 1 lessa = 144 sq ft.
- **Madhya Pradesh** — 1 katha = 600 sq ft.
- **Uttarakhand** — 1 nali = 2,160 sq ft (240 gaj); 1 mutthi = 135 sq ft.
- **Punjab** — 1 sarsai = 30.25 sq ft; 9 sarsai make a marla.
- **Andhra Pradesh & Telangana** — 1 ankanam = 72 sq ft; 1 kuncham = 4,356 sq ft (10 cents).

#### Why sizes differ — and what to rely on

Bigha, biswa and katha are older than any national standard, and each region kept its own. Many places even have two: a larger **pucca** bigha used in records and a smaller **kaccha** bigha used in everyday talk.

Government records are kept in **hectares** (or acres), and sale deeds are registered in square metres or hectares. For a purchase, loan or mutation, take the area from the record of rights — khatauni, jamabandi, 7/12 extract or patta — and confirm the local unit with the lekhpal, patwari or tehsil office. Then type that size here so the conversion matches.

#### Formulas

- Plot area in sq ft = length (ft) × width (ft).
- Gaj (sq yd) = sq ft ÷ 9.
- Square metres = sq ft ÷ 10.7639.
- Acres = sq ft ÷ 43,560. Hectares = sq ft ÷ 1,07,639.
- Bigha = sq ft ÷ the bigha of your state — for example ÷ 27,000 in Uttar Pradesh or ÷ 14,400 in West Bengal.
- Rate per bigha = rate per sq ft × sq ft in a bigha.

### Guide

#### How net salary is calculated in Luxembourg

Three things come off a gross salary: **social contributions**, **income tax** withheld by the employer, and **dependency insurance**. Tax credits are then added back. Take **€5,000 gross a month in class 1**:

Health insurance is 3.05% (€152.50) and pension insurance 8.5% (€425.00). Both are deductible, so tax is worked out on 5,000 − 152.50 − 425.00 = €4,422.50, rounded down to **€4,420**. The class 1 formula for that bracket is 38% × 4,420 − 1,006.85 = €672.70, plus the 7% employment-fund surcharge: **€719.70**.

Dependency insurance is 1.4% of the gross above a quarter of the minimum wage: 1.4% × (5,000 − 692.83) = €60.30. Finally the CIS (€25.00) and CI-CO2 (€9.00) tax credits are added. **Net: 5,000 − 152.50 − 425.00 − 719.70 − 60.30 + 34.00 = €3,676.50.**

#### Net salary in Luxembourg by tax class (2026)

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| Contribution | Employee | Employer | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

#### Tax classes 1, 1a and 2

- **Class 1** — single people without a child in the household.
- **Class 1a** — single parents with a child in the household, widowed people, and anyone aged 64 or over on 1 January. Tax starts at a higher salary than in class 1, then rises faster.
- **Class 2** — married couples taxed jointly, and for three years after being widowed, divorced or separated. The scale is applied to half the income and doubled, which is why class 2 pays far less at the same salary.
- Registered partners are withheld in their own class during the year and can ask for joint taxation in their tax return.
- Married non-residents are in class 1 unless they ask to be treated as residents; their card then shows a withholding rate instead of a class.

#### Tax credits on the payslip

- **CIS** (crédit d’impôt pour salariés) — €600 a year for a gross salary between €11,266 and €40,000, less above, nothing from €80,000.
- **CI-CO2** — €216 a year in 2026 up to €40,000 gross, tapering to nothing at €80,000. It offsets the CO2 tax.
- **CISSM** (minimum-wage credit) — €81 a month for a full-time gross of €1,800 to €3,000, tapering to nothing at €3,600; prorated for part-time work.
- **CIM** (single-parent credit) — €3,504 a year below €60,000 of taxable income, falling to €750 from €105,000. Class 1a only, on request.

#### What is not included

- Benefits in kind such as a company car, meal vouchers or housing, and the tax relief on overtime.
- A withholding rate printed on the tax card — a spouse’s second card, or a non-resident treated as a resident.
- The profit-sharing bonus and impatriate regimes, and deductions you claim only in a tax return.
- Maintenance payments, which reduce the single-parent credit.
- This is an estimate for information. Your payslip and the tax office’s assessment are what count.

### FAQ

**Where does Luxembourg Salary Calculator run?**
Luxembourg Salary Calculator runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**How much is €5,000 gross net in Luxembourg?**
In 2026, **€5,000 gross a month is €3,676.50 net in tax class 1**, €3,885.30 in class 1a and €4,155.80 in class 2 — before any travel allowance, which adds a little more.

**What is the minimum wage in Luxembourg in 2026?**
From 1 June 2026 the minimum social wage is **€2,771.33 gross a month** for an unskilled worker aged 18 or over and **€3,325.60** for a skilled worker (full time, index 992.24). The unskilled minimum is about **€2,418 net** in class 1, helped by the €81 minimum-wage tax credit.

**Which tax class am I in?**
Class 1 if you are single without children; class 1a if you are a single parent, widowed, or 64 or over on 1 January; class 2 if you are married and taxed jointly. It is printed on the tax card your employer receives from the tax administration.

**How is a 13th month taxed?**
It is ordinary salary: it pays pension, dependency and 2.8% health insurance, and is taxed at your top rate because it comes on top of the year’s other pay. On €5,000 a month in class 1 you keep about €2,423 of a €5,000 13th month.

**Does this work for cross-border workers?**
Yes for the Luxembourg payslip: frontaliers pay the same contributions and the same withholding tax on salary earned in Luxembourg. Days worked from home beyond the treaty limit (34 a year for Belgium, France and Germany) are taxed in your country of residence instead, which this calculator does not model.

**Is the pension contribution 8% or 8.5%?**
It is **8.5%** for the employee and 8.5% for the employer since 1 January 2026. It was 8% each until the end of 2025.

**Why is my real payslip a little different?**
Usually because of benefits in kind, overtime, a different travel allowance or extra deductions on your tax card, or because the month had back pay or a bonus. Enter the distance and deductions from your card to get closer.

**Is my salary stored or sent anywhere?**
No. The calculation runs in this tab and nothing you type is uploaded.

## GPA & CGPA Calculator

GPA & CGPA Calculator on Toolspire: Calculate SGPA, GPA and CGPA from credits and grades, convert CGPA to percentage with your university’s formula.

### At a glance

- GPA & CGPA Calculator on Toolspire: calculates **SGPA (semester GPA)** from each course’s credits and grade: Σ(credits × grade points) ÷ Σ credits, rounded to two decimals.
- Calculates **CGPA** across semesters — credit-weighted when you enter credits — and reproduces the worked examples in the UGC’s credit-system guidelines.
- Supports the **UGC 10-point scale** (O = 10, A+ = 9, A = 8, B+ = 7, B = 6, C = 5, P = 4, F = 0), the **US 4.0 scale** with Honors and AP weighting, and a 5-point scale — or type grade points directly.
- Converts **CGPA to percentage** and back with the formula your university uses: CGPA × 9.5, CGPA × 10, (CGPA − 0.75) × 10, (CGPA − 0.5) × 10, 7.1 × CGPA + 11, or your own.
- An **8.2 CGPA** is 77.9% with CGPA × 9.5, 82% with CGPA × 10 and 74.5% with (CGPA − 0.75) × 10.
- **Target planner**: the average SGPA you need in the remaining semesters to reach a goal CGPA, and the highest CGPA still possible.
- Your courses and semesters are saved on your device only; nothing is uploaded.

### Features

- **SGPA from credits and grades**: Add your courses, pick a letter grade or type grade points, and see the working.
- **CGPA across semesters**: Enter each semester’s SGPA and credits — or send a finished semester over with one tap.
- **CGPA to percentage**: Formulas commonly used by CBSE, DU, VTU, AKTU, Anna, GTU, KTU, MAKAUT, JNTUH and Mumbai University — or your own.
- **Target CGPA planner**: Find the average you need from here, and whether the goal is still within reach.
- **US GPA too**: The 4.0 scale with plus and minus grades, and weighted GPA for Honors, AP and IB courses.
- **Saved for next semester**: Your entries stay in this tab, ready when the next results come out.

### How to calculate SGPA and CGPA

1. **Pick your grading scale** — Choose the 10-point scale used in India, the US 4.0 scale or a 5-point scale.
2. **Enter your courses** — For each course type the credits and choose the grade. If your university uses different letters, switch to **Grade points** and type the number from your marksheet.
3. **Read your SGPA** — The SGPA appears with the total credits and credit points. Tap **Add to CGPA** to carry it over as a semester.
4. **Get your CGPA** — On the **CGPA** tab enter the SGPA and credits of every semester to get your cumulative figure.
5. **Convert or plan** — Use **CGPA to %** with your university’s formula, or **Target** to see what you need in the semesters left.

### Guide

#### SGPA and CGPA formulas

**SGPA = Σ(credits × grade points) ÷ Σ credits** for the courses of one semester. Each course’s grade points are multiplied by its credits, so a 4-credit course counts twice as much as a 2-credit one.

**CGPA = Σ(semester credits × SGPA) ÷ Σ credits** over all semesters so far. The UGC’s own illustration: six semesters of 20, 20, 26, 26, 24 and 24 credits with SGPAs of 6.9, 6.7, 9.15, 7.38, 7.75 and 8.0 give (20 × 6.9 + 20 × 6.7 + 26 × 9.15 + 26 × 7.38 + 24 × 7.75 + 24 × 8.0) ÷ 140 = **7.71**.

| Course | Credits | Grade | Grade points | Credit points |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mathematics | 4 | O | 10 | 40 |
| Physics | 4 | A+ | 9 | 36 |
| Programming | 3 | A | 8 | 24 |
| English | 2 | B+ | 7 | 14 |
| Physics lab | 2 | O | 10 | 20 |
| Total | 15 |  |  | 134 → SGPA 8.93 |

#### UGC 10-point grading scale

The letter grades and grade points the University Grants Commission recommends for the choice-based credit system. Universities set their own marks ranges for each grade.

| Letter grade | Grade points | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| O | 10 | Outstanding |
| A+ | 9 | Excellent |
| A | 8 | Very good |
| B+ | 7 | Good |
| B | 6 | Above average |
| C | 5 | Average |
| P | 4 | Pass |
| F | 0 | Fail |
| Ab | 0 | Absent |

#### CGPA to percentage formulas

There is no single national rule: each board and university publishes its own conversion, and some change it between schemes — KTU, for example, moved from 10 × CGPA − 2.5 to CGPA × 10 in 2023. The table shows the formulas commonly reported. **Use the one printed on your marksheet or in your university’s circular**; that is what employers and admission offices accept.

| Formula | Commonly used by | 8.2 CGPA becomes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CGPA × 9.5 | CBSE (Class 10 CGPA), Delhi University | 77.9% |
| CGPA × 10 | Anna University, KTU and many others | 82% |
| (CGPA − 0.75) × 10 | VTU, AKTU, MAKAUT | 74.5% |
| (CGPA − 0.5) × 10 | GTU, JNTU Hyderabad | 77% |
| 7.1 × CGPA + 11 | Mumbai University | 69.22% |
| 7.25 × CGPA + 11 | Mumbai University | 70.45% |

#### US GPA on the 4.0 scale

An A is 4.0, A− 3.7, B+ 3.3, B 3.0, B− 2.7, C+ 2.3, C 2.0, C− 1.7, D+ 1.3, D 1.0, D− 0.7 and F 0. GPA is the credit-weighted average, exactly like SGPA.

A **weighted GPA** adds 0.5 for an Honors course and 1.0 for an AP or IB course, so it can go above 4.0. Colleges usually look at both. Schools differ on the details — some count A+ as 4.3 — so check your school’s handbook.

#### SGPA, CGPA and GPA — what is the difference?

- **SGPA** (semester grade point average) covers the courses of one semester.
- **CGPA** (cumulative grade point average) covers every semester completed so far.
- **GPA** is the general term, and the one used in the US; a semester GPA is the same idea as an SGPA.
- Some universities call the same figures SPI and CPI, or GPA and CGPI.

#### Converting an Indian CGPA to a 4.0 GPA

There is no official conversion. Dividing by 10 and multiplying by 4 gives a rough figure — an 8.0 CGPA is about 3.2 — but US universities and credential evaluators such as WES convert course by course from your marks, so their figure can differ a good deal. When applying abroad, report your CGPA on its own scale unless the form asks otherwise.

### FAQ

**Where does GPA & CGPA Calculator run?**
GPA & CGPA Calculator runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**How do I calculate SGPA?**
Multiply each course’s credits by its grade points, add those up, and divide by the total credits. Five courses worth 15 credits with 134 credit points give 134 ÷ 15 = **8.93**.

**How do I calculate CGPA from SGPA?**
Multiply each semester’s SGPA by its credits, add the results, and divide by the total credits. If every semester has the same credits, the CGPA is simply the average of the SGPAs.

**How do I convert CGPA to percentage?**
It depends on your university. Common formulas are **CGPA × 9.5** (CBSE, Delhi University), **CGPA × 10** (Anna University, KTU), **(CGPA − 0.75) × 10** (VTU, AKTU, MAKAUT) and **(CGPA − 0.5) × 10** (GTU, JNTUH). An 8.2 CGPA is 77.9%, 82%, 74.5% or 77% respectively — check your marksheet for the right one.

**Why is CGPA multiplied by 9.5?**
CBSE set 9.5 as the factor for the CGPA it printed on Class 10 marksheets, so a perfect 10 CGPA corresponds to 95%. Many colleges borrowed the same factor, but it is not a universal rule.

**What SGPA do I need to reach my target CGPA?**
Use the **Target** tab. For example, with a 7.5 CGPA after 80 credits, finishing on 8.0 after another 80 credits needs an average of 8.5 from here. If the answer is above 10, the target is out of reach and the calculator shows the best CGPA still possible.

**Does a failed course count in SGPA and CGPA?**
Yes — an F carries 0 grade points and its credits still count, which pulls the average down. Most universities replace it with the new grade once you clear the backlog; enter the grade that appears on your latest marksheet.

**What is the difference between weighted and unweighted GPA?**
An unweighted GPA treats every course the same, on a 4.0 scale. A weighted GPA adds 0.5 for Honors and 1.0 for AP or IB courses to reward harder classes, so it can exceed 4.0.

**Is my data stored?**
Only on your own device. Your courses, semesters and chosen formula are kept in this tab’s local storage so they are there next time; **Clear** removes them. Nothing is sent to a server.

## GST Calculator

URL: https://justtools.info/calculators/gst-calculator/

GST Calculator on Toolspire. GST calculator for India: add or remove GST at 5%, 18% or 40%, split CGST, SGST and IGST.

### At a glance

- GST Calculator on Toolspire: **Adds GST** to a price or **removes GST** from a price that already includes it, at the current slabs of **5%, 18% and 40%** — plus 0%, 0.25%, 1.5% and 3%, and the old 12% and 28% for earlier bills.
- Splits the tax into **CGST + SGST** for a sale within one state, or **IGST** for a sale to another state.
- **₹10,000 + 18% GST = ₹11,800** (CGST ₹900 + SGST ₹900). Taking 18% GST out of ₹10,000 leaves **₹8,474.58** before tax and ₹1,525.42 of GST.
- Totals a **bill with several items at different rates**, with a rate-wise summary of taxable value, CGST, SGST or IGST, and round-off — downloadable as CSV.
- Works out the **GST payable after input tax credit**: the tax on a sale less the tax already paid on the purchase.
- Has a **GST rate finder** for over 90 everyday goods and services, with the rates in force since **22 September 2025** (and tobacco at 40% since 1 February 2026).
- Shows the working and the amount in words. Everything runs in this tab; nothing is uploaded.

### Features

- **Add or remove GST**: From a price before tax to the total, or from an MRP or bill total back to the taxable value.
- **CGST, SGST, IGST**: Equal CGST and SGST for a sale in the same state, IGST across states — rounded to the paisa.
- **Current 2026 slabs**: 5%, 18% and 40% one tap away, with the special 3% for gold and the old 12% and 28% for past invoices.
- **Multi-item bill**: Up to 30 items, each with its own quantity, price and rate, prices with or without GST.
- **Input tax credit**: See the net GST a registered seller actually pays, and the profit on the deal.

### How to calculate GST

1. **Choose add or remove** — Pick **Add GST** if your price is before tax, or **Remove GST** if the price already includes it.
2. **Enter the amount** — Type the price in rupees.
3. **Pick the GST rate** — Tap 5%, 18% or 40%, type any other rate, or search the **rate finder** below for your product.
4. **Choose the type of sale** — Keep **The same state** for CGST + SGST, or switch to **Different states** for IGST.
5. **Read the result** — See the taxable value, each tax and the total, with the working and the amount in words. Copy it, or build a full bill below.

### Guide

#### GST calculation formulas

**To add GST:** GST = price × rate ÷ 100, and total = price + GST. For ₹10,000 at 18%: GST = 10,000 × 18 ÷ 100 = ₹1,800, so the total is **₹11,800**.

**To remove GST (reverse calculation):** value before GST = total ÷ (1 + rate ÷ 100), and GST = total − value. For a ₹11,800 bill at 18%: 11,800 ÷ 1.18 = **₹10,000**, so the GST inside it is ₹1,800.

Do not simply take the percentage off the total. 18% of ₹11,800 is ₹2,124 — too much, because GST is charged on the value before tax, not on the total.

#### GST rates in 2026

Since 22 September 2025 GST has two main slabs, a merit rate of 5% and a standard rate of 18%, and a 40% rate for a short list of luxury and sin goods. The 12% and 28% slabs were abolished.

| GST rate | What it covers |
| --- | --- |
| Nil | Fresh food, milk, bread and roti, paneer, notebooks and pencils, individual health and life insurance, 36 life-saving medicines |
| 0.25% / 1.5% | Rough diamonds / cut and polished diamonds |
| 3% | Gold, silver, platinum and jewellery |
| 5% | Packaged food, butter and ghee, toothpaste, soap and shampoo, medicines, clothes and footwear up to ₹2,500, tractors, bicycles, hotel rooms up to ₹7,500, gyms and salons |
| 18% | The standard rate: mobile phones, laptops, TVs, air conditioners, cement, small cars, motorcycles up to 350 cc, and most services |
| 40% | Aerated and energy drinks, larger cars and SUVs, motorcycles above 350 cc, yachts, betting and casinos, cigarettes and pan masala |

#### How much of an inclusive price is GST?

When a price already includes GST, the tax is a smaller share of it than the rate suggests. Divide the price by the number in the last column to get the value before tax.

| GST rate | GST as a share of the inclusive price | Divide the price by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 3% | 2.91% | 1.03 |
| 5% | 4.76% | 1.05 |
| 12% (old) | 10.71% | 1.12 |
| 18% | 15.25% | 1.18 |
| 28% (old) | 21.88% | 1.28 |
| 40% | 28.57% | 1.40 |

#### CGST, SGST and IGST

- **CGST** (central GST) and **SGST** (state GST) apply together to a sale within one state. Each is half the rate: 18% GST is 9% CGST + 9% SGST.
- **UTGST** replaces SGST in union territories without a legislature, such as Chandigarh and Ladakh.
- **IGST** (integrated GST) applies to a sale from one state to another, and to imports. It is the full rate as one tax: 18% IGST.
- The total tax is the same either way — only where the money goes differs.

#### What changed with GST 2.0

The GST Council’s 56th meeting on 3 September 2025 replaced the four slabs of 5%, 12%, 18% and 28% with **5% and 18%**, plus **40%** for a few goods. Most 12% items moved to 5%, and most 28% items — air conditioners, large TVs, cement, small cars, motorcycles up to 350 cc — moved to 18%. The new rates apply from **22 September 2025**.

The **compensation cess** on cars, aerated drinks and coal ended on the same day, which is why larger cars are now a flat 40% instead of 28% plus cess. Cigarettes, pan masala and other tobacco products moved to 40% on **1 February 2026**, charged on the printed retail price, with a separate excise duty or health cess on top.

#### Input tax credit

A GST-registered business does not pay the whole GST it collects. It deducts the GST it paid on its own purchases — the **input tax credit** — and pays the difference. Buy goods for ₹10,000 + ₹1,800 GST and sell them for ₹12,000 + ₹2,160 GST: the tax to pay is 2,160 − 1,800 = **₹360**, which is 18% of the ₹2,000 of value added.

### FAQ

**Where does GST Calculator run?**
GST Calculator runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**How do I calculate GST on an amount?**
Multiply the amount by the GST rate and divide by 100. For ₹5,000 at 18%: 5,000 × 18 ÷ 100 = ₹900 of GST, so the total is ₹5,900. Within a state that is ₹450 CGST + ₹450 SGST.

**How do I remove GST from a total?**
Divide the total by 1 + the rate: by **1.05** for 5%, **1.18** for 18%, **1.40** for 40%. A ₹5,900 bill at 18% is 5,900 ÷ 1.18 = ₹5,000 before GST, with ₹900 of tax. Choose **Remove GST** above to do it automatically.

**What are the GST rates in 2026?**
The main slabs are **5%** and **18%**, with **40%** on a short list of luxury and sin goods. Essentials are nil-rated, gold and silver are 3%, and diamonds 0.25% or 1.5%. The 12% and 28% slabs ended on 22 September 2025.

**Is 12% or 28% GST still charged?**
Not on new sales. Those slabs were abolished on 22 September 2025 — tobacco products stayed at 28% plus cess until 1 February 2026 and are now 40%. Both rates are still offered here so you can check older invoices.

**What is the difference between CGST, SGST and IGST?**
CGST and SGST are charged together, half the rate each, when buyer and seller are in the same state. IGST is charged alone, at the full rate, when they are in different states or the goods are imported.

**What is the GST on mobile phones, gold and cars?**
Mobile phones are **18%**. Gold and silver jewellery is **3%**, with 5% on making charges. Small cars are **18%**; larger cars and SUVs are **40%**; electric vehicles are 5%. Search the rate finder above for other items.

**How is GST rounded?**
Each tax is rounded to the nearest paisa, and CGST and SGST are always equal — so when GST is taken out of a price within a state, the value before tax can sit one paisa below price ÷ (1 + rate). Many businesses then round the bill total to the nearest rupee: switch on **Round off the total** in the bill section.

**Is anything I enter stored or uploaded?**
No. The calculation happens in this tab and nothing is sent to a server.

### How to make an exam seating arrangement

1. **Add your students** — Create one group for each class, section or subject in the session. Type roll-number ranges such as **1-40**, or choose **Paste a list** for roll numbers with names.
2. **Add your rooms** — For each room enter the rows of desks, the desks across and the seats on each desk. The number of seats is shown as you type.
3. **Choose how to mix** — Keep **Side by side and front–back** for a checkerboard, or pick another rule. Choose whether seats are numbered down each column or along each row.
4. **Check the plan** — Read the message above the chart: it says whether everyone has a seat and whether any classmates still sit together. Tap **Mark seats not in use** for broken desks.
5. **Print** — Print the seating charts, attendance sheets, notice-board list and desk slips, or download the plan as CSV.

### Guide

#### How the seats are filled

Seats are numbered along a path — down each column of seats, or along each row — and filled in that order. At every seat the planner takes the next student from the group that clashes least with the neighbours already seated, and prefers the group with the most students still waiting, so the groups run out together.

Clashes are ranked: two classmates **on the same desk** are avoided first, then **side by side across an aisle**, then **front and back**, then **diagonally**. Within a group, students keep the order you entered, so roll numbers still run in sequence along the path and are easy to find.

A second pass swaps seats where that removes a clash that was left over. If a clash cannot be avoided — for example when one class is more than half the room — the planner tells you how many pairs remain instead of hiding them.

#### Which rule to choose

| Rule | Who is kept apart | Groups needed | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Side by side only | Desk-mates and side neighbours | 2 | Each column is one class — easy for handing out papers |
| Side by side and front–back | The four nearest seats | 2 | A checkerboard; the usual choice |
| All around, diagonals too | All eight surrounding seats | 4 | The strictest plan, for high-stakes exams |
| Don’t mix | Nobody | 1 | One class after another |

#### How many students fit in a room

Seats = rows × desks across × seats per desk. Take away any seats you mark as not in use.

| Rows | Desks across | Seats per desk | Seats |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5 | 4 | 2 | 40 |
| 6 | 5 | 2 | 60 |
| 8 | 5 | 2 | 80 |
| 10 | 6 | 2 | 120 |
| 6 | 5 | 1 | 30 |
| 6 | 4 | 3 | 72 |

#### What to print

- **Seating charts** — the room seen from above, with every roll number in its seat. One page per room, for the door and the invigilator. Wide rooms print in landscape.
- **Attendance sheets** — seat, roll number, name, group and a signature box for each student, room by room.
- **Notice-board list** — for each class, which roll numbers go to which room, so students find their room at a glance.
- **Desk slips** — a label for each seat with the roll number, room and seat number, to cut out and stick on desks.

#### Tips for a fair seating plan

- Seat at least two classes or subjects in every session; a single class can only be spaced out, not mixed.
- For a clean checkerboard no group should be more than half the seats in use. If one is, add a room so that spare seats can act as gaps.
- Keep a few spare seats in every room for late changes, and mark broken desks before printing.
- Use **Shuffled** order for class tests where friends would otherwise sit in roll-number order near each other.
- Print the notice-board list the day before, and the charts and attendance sheets on the day.

**How do I make sure no two students of the same class sit together?**
Seat two or more classes in the same room and keep the rule on **Side by side and front–back**. The planner alternates the classes like a checkerboard. It works fully when no class is more than half of the seats used; otherwise it shows how many pairs could not be separated.

## Mic Tester

Mic Tester on Toolspire. Test your microphone online: a live sound level, waveform and spectrum, record and play back a clip, and fix a mic that is muted.

### At a glance

- Mic Tester on Toolspire: tests a **microphone in this tab**: press the button, allow access, and a live level meter shows at once whether sound is coming in.
- Says plainly what it hears — **working**, **no sound**, **too quiet**, **too loud** or **distorting** — and what to do about each.
- Shows the **level in decibels (dBFS)**, the loudest peak, the background noise, a live **waveform** and **frequency spectrum**, and the main pitch.

- Lets you **choose between microphones** and switch echo cancellation, noise suppression and automatic gain on or off.
- Works with built-in, USB, Bluetooth and headset microphones on Windows, Mac, Linux, Chromebook, Android, iPhone and iPad.
- The sound is analysed on your device. Nothing is uploaded or stored; a recording stays in the tab until you close it.

### Features

- **A clear verdict**: Not just a moving bar: the test tells you whether the microphone works and what is wrong if it does not.
- **Record and play back**: Hear your own voice as a call or recording would capture it.
- **Pick the right device**: Switch between laptop, headset and USB microphones without leaving the page.
- **Waveform and spectrum**: See the sound wave live, or the frequencies from bass to treble.
- **Processing on or off**: Compare the microphone with and without noise suppression, echo cancellation and auto gain.
- **Private**: No account, no upload. Audio never leaves your browser.

### How to test your microphone

1. **Start the test** — Press **Test my microphone**. When the browser asks, choose **Allow**.
2. **Speak** — Talk at your normal voice. The meter should move and the message should change to **Your microphone is working**.
3. **Check the device** — If nothing moves, pick another device under **Microphone** — the browser may be listening to the wrong one.
4. **Record a clip** — Press **Record**, say a sentence, then play it back to hear the quality.

### Guide

#### What the level means

The meter is in dBFS — decibels below the loudest sound a digital recording can hold. 0 dB is the ceiling; quieter sounds are negative numbers.

| Peak level | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| 0 dB | The ceiling. Sound that reaches it is cut off and distorts — lower the input volume. |
| −12 to −3 dB | Strong and clear. Where a confident voice close to the microphone peaks. |
| −30 to −12 dB | Normal speech. Fine for calls and recordings. |
| Below −30 dB | Quiet. Others may struggle to hear you — move closer or raise the input volume. |
| Below −60 dB | Silence, or background noise only. |

#### Microphone not working? Check these

- **Permission** — the browser must be allowed to use the microphone for this site. Click the icon at the left of the address bar and set Microphone to Allow.
- **The right device** — laptops with a headset or webcam attached have several microphones. Choose the one you are speaking into.
- **Mute** — look for a mute switch on the headset cable or boom, and the microphone-mute key on the keyboard.
- **Input volume** — in Windows open Settings → System → Sound → Input; on a Mac, System Settings → Sound → Input. Raise the level and watch the meter there.
- **Privacy settings** — Windows and macOS can block the microphone for all apps or for your browser. Switch it on under Privacy & security → Microphone.
- **Another app** — close Zoom, Teams, Meet or a recorder that may be holding the microphone, then try again.
- **Bluetooth** — a Bluetooth headset must be connected in its call or "hands-free" mode for its microphone to work.
- **The cable** — unplug it and plug it in again, and try another USB port or the other audio socket.

#### Echo cancellation, noise suppression and auto gain

Browsers clean up microphone sound before an app gets it. **Echo cancellation** removes the sound of your own speakers, **noise suppression** removes steady background noise such as a fan, and **automatic gain** raises a quiet voice and lowers a loud one.

Video-call apps keep all three on, so that is how the test starts. Switch them off to hear the microphone as it really is — useful for music, podcasts, or working out whether a thin or "underwater" sound comes from the microphone or from the processing.

#### Works here but not in your call?

If this test hears you but Zoom, Google Meet or Microsoft Teams does not, the microphone itself is fine. The app is usually using a different microphone, or you are muted inside it. Open the app’s audio settings and select the same device that worked here.

### FAQ

**Where does Mic Tester run?**
Mic Tester runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**How do I test my microphone?**
Press **Test my microphone**, allow access when the browser asks, and speak. If the meter moves and you see **Your microphone is working**, it is fine. Record a short clip to check how you sound.

**Why is my microphone not working?**
The usual causes are a blocked permission in the browser, the wrong input device being selected, a hardware mute switch, or the input volume set to zero. Work through the checklist on this page from top to bottom.

**How can I hear myself?**
Record a clip and play it back — that is the truest test. You can also switch on **Hear yourself** to listen live; wear headphones, or the speakers will feed back into the microphone.

**What is a good microphone level?**
Speech that peaks between about −30 and −3 dB is healthy. Below −30 dB you are quiet; at 0 dB the sound clips and distorts.

**Why does my voice sound muffled or robotic?**
That is usually noise suppression working hard against background noise, or a Bluetooth headset in call mode. Switch noise suppression off here to compare, and move away from fans and open windows.

**Can I test a headset or AirPods microphone?**
Yes. Connect them, start the test and choose them in the **Microphone** list. Bluetooth earbuds switch to a lower-quality call mode while their microphone is in use — that is normal.

**Is my voice recorded or uploaded?**
No. The sound is measured inside your browser and nothing is sent anywhere. A recording you make stays in this tab and disappears when you close it, unless you download it.

**Does it work on a phone?**
Yes — in Chrome on Android and Safari on iPhone and iPad. Open the page in the browser itself; in-app browsers such as Instagram’s often block the microphone.

## Webcam Tester

URL: https://justtools.info/device-tests/webcam-test/
Category: Device Tests
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-13

Webcam Tester on Toolspire. Test your webcam online: see the live picture, resolution, megapixels and frame rate, take a photo or record a clip.

### At a glance

- Webcam Tester on Toolspire: tests a **webcam in this tab**: press the button, allow access, and the live picture appears with its resolution and frame rate.
- Reports the **real resolution** (for example 1920 × 1080, Full HD), **megapixels**, **aspect ratio** and the **frames per second** actually arriving — measured, not just what the camera claims.
- Asks the camera for its **best mode**, so a Full HD webcam is not tested at the 640 × 480 that browsers often start with.
- Judges the **lighting** — too dark, well lit or washed out — and warns when the picture is black because of a lens cover.
- **Takes a photo** (PNG at full resolution) and **records a clip** of up to 30 seconds to play back and download.
- Lets you **choose between cameras**, try each standard resolution, mirror the preview, show grid lines and go full screen.
- The picture stays on your device. Nothing is uploaded or stored.

### Features

- **True resolution and FPS**: What the camera delivers right now, with a plain rating for video calls.
- **Lighting check**: Brightness is measured from the picture, with a tip when it is too dark or too bright.
- **Photo and video**: Take a full-resolution snapshot or record a short clip, and download either.
- **Every camera**: Switch between built-in, USB and phone front and back cameras.
- **Mirror and grid**: Preview yourself mirrored like a video call, with rule-of-thirds lines to frame the shot.
- **Private**: No account, no upload. The video never leaves your browser.

### How to test your webcam

1. **Start the test** — Press **Test my webcam**. When the browser asks, choose **Allow**.
2. **Look at the picture** — You should see yourself. The badge on the picture shows the resolution and frames per second.
3. **Check the details** — Read the rating, the lighting advice and the camera’s maximum resolution beside the picture.
4. **Try a photo or clip** — Press **Take a photo** or **Record a clip** to see the quality others will get.

### Guide

#### Webcam resolutions

The resolution is the number of pixels in each frame. More pixels give a sharper picture, as long as there is enough light.

| Name | Pixels | Megapixels | Shape |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4K UHD | 3840 × 2160 | 8.3 MP | 16:9 |
| QHD 1440p | 2560 × 1440 | 3.7 MP | 16:9 |
| Full HD 1080p | 1920 × 1080 | 2.1 MP | 16:9 |
| HD 720p | 1280 × 720 | 0.9 MP | 16:9 |
| VGA 480p | 640 × 480 | 0.3 MP | 4:3 |
| QVGA 240p | 320 × 240 | 0.1 MP | 4:3 |

#### What is good enough for video calls?

- **Full HD (1080p) at 24 fps or more** — excellent. More than a call needs; right for streaming and recording.
- **HD (720p) at 20 fps or more** — good. What most video calls actually send.
- **480p** — basic. Fine on a phone-sized window, soft on a large screen.
- Below 12 frames a second the picture looks jerky. Low frame rates are usually caused by poor light: the camera slows down to gather more of it.

#### Webcam not working? Check these

- **Permission** — click the icon at the left of the address bar and set Camera to Allow, then try again.
- **Privacy shutter** — many laptops have a sliding cover over the lens or a camera key (often F8 or F10). A black picture usually means it is closed.
- **Another app** — only one app can use most cameras at a time. Close Zoom, Teams, Meet or the Camera app.
- **Privacy settings** — in Windows and macOS, switch on camera access for your browser under Privacy & security → Camera.
- **The right camera** — choose the camera you want from the list; a virtual camera from another program may have been picked.
- **The cable** — for a USB webcam, unplug it and plug it into another port, directly rather than through a hub.

#### Look better on camera

- Face the light. A window or lamp in front of you beats one behind you.
- Raise the camera to eye level and sit an arm’s length away.
- Wipe the lens — a fingerprint makes the whole picture hazy.
- Use the grid: put your eyes on the upper line.

### FAQ

**Where does Webcam Tester run?**
Webcam Tester runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**How do I test my webcam?**
Press **Test my webcam** and allow access when the browser asks. If you see yourself, the camera works; the page also shows its resolution, frame rate and how well lit the picture is.

**Why is my webcam showing a black screen?**
Usually the lens is covered by a privacy shutter, the camera is switched off with a keyboard key, or another app is using it. The test warns you when the picture is completely black.

**How do I check my webcam’s resolution?**
Start the test: the resolution is shown on the picture and under **About this camera**, with the megapixels and the camera’s maximum. Use **Resolution to test** to try 720p, 1080p or 4K.

**Why is the picture mirrored?**
The preview is flipped like a mirror because that feels natural, as in video-call apps. Other people — and the photos you take here — see you the right way round. Switch **Mirror the preview** off to see that view.

**Why is my frame rate low?**
In dim light a webcam lengthens its exposure and delivers fewer frames. Add light in front of you. A slow USB hub or a high resolution on an old computer can also hold it back.

**Can I test my phone’s camera?**
Yes. Open this page in Chrome on Android or Safari on iPhone, start the test, and switch between the front and back cameras in the **Camera** list.

**Is the video recorded or uploaded?**
No. The picture goes from the camera to your screen inside the browser. A photo or clip you make stays in this tab until you close it, unless you download it.

**Does this test the microphone too?**
No — clips recorded here are picture only. Use the [Mic Tester](https://justtools.info/device-tests/mic-test/) for sound.

## Speaker Tester

URL: https://justtools.info/device-tests/speaker-test/
Category: Device Tests
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-22

Speaker Tester on Toolspire. Play a tone in the left speaker, the right, or both, then sweep from bass to treble.

### At a glance

- Speaker Tester on Toolspire: plays a **sine tone** at 250 Hz, 440 Hz, 1 kHz, 4 kHz and 8 kHz, plus a **6-second sweep** from 80 Hz to 8 kHz.
- Can send the tone to the **left channel, the right channel, or both**, so a dead earpiece or a reversed headphone plug shows up at once.
- The loudness slider is capped well below full scale. A pure tone sounds much louder than a song at the same setting.
- Sound is generated with the Web Audio API **in this tab**. Nothing is recorded and nothing is uploaded.
- Works with built-in speakers, headphones, USB DACs and Bluetooth headsets in current desktop and mobile browsers.

### Features

- **Left and right**: A tone that should come from only one side. If it comes from the other, the plug or the balance is reversed.
- **Five reference tones**: Bass, the note A4, speech range, clarity and treble — enough to hear a rattle or a missing driver.
- **Log sweep**: Glides from low to high so a buzz at one frequency is easy to catch.
- **Safe volume**: The loudest setting is still a modest sine, and every tone fades in and out instead of clicking.

### How to test your speakers

1. **Put headphones on** — Headphones make left and right obvious. Desk speakers work too — sit in the middle.
2. **Set a comfortable volume** — Start near 40%. A test tone is louder than it looks.
3. **Play Left, then Right** — You should hear each side on its own. If both ears hear “Left only”, the balance or the cable is wrong.
4. **Run the sweep** — Listen for a buzz, a drop-out or a frequency that is much louder than the rest.

### Guide

#### What each tone is for

| Tone | Listen for |
| --- | --- |
| 250 Hz | Bass and rattles in a loose panel or a phone case. |
| 440 Hz | A familiar musical A. Useful as a level match between two speakers. |
| 1 kHz | The middle of speech. A speaker that is weak here sounds muffled on calls. |
| 4 kHz | Consonants and detail. Missing treble shows up here first. |
| 8 kHz | Air and hiss. Many small laptop speakers barely reach this. |

#### Only one side plays

- **Balance** — Windows: Settings → System → Sound → the speaker → right-hand pane, or the volume mixer. Mac: System Settings → Sound → Output → Balance.
- **The plug** — a headphone jack that is not pushed all the way in often drops one channel.
- **Mono accessory** — some Bluetooth headsets and phone earpieces are mono. The test will still play, but left and right will sound the same.
- **The app** — if a call app is holding the output in “voice” mode, quit it and play the tone again.

### FAQ

**Where does Speaker Tester run?**
Speaker Tester runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**How do I test my left and right speakers?**
Choose **Left** and play any tone, then **Right**. Each tone should come from only that side. Choose **Both** to hear them together.

**Why is the test tone so loud?**
A pure sine has all of its energy at one frequency, so it sounds sharper than music at the same volume. The slider never reaches full scale, and you can turn it down before you press play.

**The sweep buzzes at one point. Is the speaker broken?**
A short buzz often means something loose — a grille, a desk, or a phone case — vibrating at that frequency. Hold the speaker and try again. A tone that disappears entirely can mean a damaged driver.

**Does this test record my room?**
No. It only plays sound. It does not open the microphone, and it does not upload anything.

**Why do left and right sound the same on my phone?**
The phone’s own speaker is usually a single driver. Plug in headphones to hear a real stereo image.

## Keyboard Tester

URL: https://justtools.info/device-tests/keyboard-test/
Category: Device Tests
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-22

Press every key and see it light up. The test marks keys that stick, counts repeats, and never sends what you type anywhere. Open Keyboard Tester on Toolspire.

### At a glance

- Keyboard Tester on Toolspire: draws a full keyboard and **lights each key** as the browser reports it, including function keys, modifiers and arrows.
- A key held for **more than 4 seconds** is called out, which is how a stuck key usually shows up.
- Counts **auto-repeat** events separately from real presses, so a chatty key is visible.
- Keeps a short list of the latest keys and their `KeyboardEvent.code`, the physical key rather than the character.
- Runs entirely in the page. Keystrokes are **not stored** and not sent anywhere. Leaving the tab releases every “held” key.

### Features

- **A key that lights up**: Pressed keys are filled in. Keys you have already tried stay tinted, so you can see what you still have not pressed.
- **Stuck-key warning**: If a key is still down after four seconds, the page says so.
- **Repeat counter**: Holding a key on purpose increments Repeats, which is also how you spot a key that chatters.
- **Physical codes**: The log shows codes such as KeyA and ShiftLeft, which stay stable across layouts.

### How to test a keyboard

1. **Click the page** — Make sure the cursor is not in a text field. Those swallow keys on purpose.
2. **Press every key once** — Each key should light up and then go dark when you release it.
3. **Watch for a key that stays lit** — A key that is still highlighted after you have let go, and that the warning names after four seconds, is sticking.
4. **Try a modifier** — Shift, Ctrl, Alt and the Windows or Command key each have their own place on the diagram.

### Guide

#### A key does nothing

- **The cursor is in a field** — click the grey page background and try again.
- **A browser shortcut** — Ctrl, Alt and Command combinations are left alone so the test does not steal refresh or tab switching. Press the key on its own.
- **Fn on a laptop** — function keys may be media keys until you hold Fn, or the other way round. That is a firmware setting, not a dead key.
- **The switch** — spill, dust or a worn switch can kill one key. If the same key fails in another app, the keyboard is the problem.

#### Code and character

The diagram uses the physical position (`KeyQ`), not the letter your layout prints. On an AZERTY keyboard the key in the Q position still reports `KeyQ` while the character is A. That is why the log shows both.

### FAQ

**Where does Keyboard Tester run?**
Keyboard Tester runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**How do I find a stuck key?**
Press and release the suspect key. If it stays lit, and the amber line names it after about four seconds, the keyboard is still sending “down” with no “up”.

**Are my keystrokes uploaded or saved?**
No. The page only remembers the last few keys in memory so it can draw them. Closing the tab clears that, and nothing is sent to a server.

**Why did Ctrl and Alt not light the letter keys?**
Shortcuts are ignored so the test does not block refresh, find, or tab switching. Press Ctrl or Alt on its own — those keys are on the bottom row.

**Does it work with a non-US layout?**
Yes. Lighting follows the physical key. The character you see in the status line follows your layout, so an AZERTY or Hindi layout still maps onto the same diagram.

**My function keys change the volume instead. Is that a fault?**
No. Laptops often make F1–F12 into media keys. Hold Fn, or switch the Fn lock in the BIOS or keyboard settings, and test them again.

## Mouse Tester

URL: https://justtools.info/device-tests/mouse-test/
Category: Device Tests
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-22

Click, right-click, scroll and double-click in the pad. The test counts each button and shows where the pointer is. Open Mouse Tester on Toolspire.

### At a glance

- Mouse Tester on Toolspire: counts **left, right, middle, back and forward** clicks inside the pad.
- A second click within **500 ms** counts as a double-click and shows the gap in milliseconds.
- Reads the **scroll wheel** and a sideways tilt, separately up, down, left and right.
- Shows the pointer position **inside the pad**, in pixels from the top-left corner.
- Nothing is uploaded. The counts live in the page until you press Reset or leave.

### Features

- **Every button**: Left, right, middle and the side buttons each have their own counter, and light up while held.
- **Double-click timing**: See whether a double-click is landing inside the usual half-second window.
- **Scroll directions**: The wheel and a horizontal tilt are counted apart, so a tired wheel is obvious.
- **A tracking pad**: Coordinates follow the pointer. If they freeze while the mouse still moves, the browser is not receiving events.

### How to test a mouse

1. **Move into the pad** — The coordinates should change as the pointer moves. They are measured from the pad’s top-left corner.
2. **Click each button** — Left, right and the wheel-click should each add one to their counter. The right-click menu is suppressed inside the pad.
3. **Double-click** — Two quick left clicks should raise the double-click count and show the gap.
4. **Roll the wheel** — Scrolling over the pad should increase the up or down count instead of moving the page.

### Guide

#### A button that never counts

- **Click inside the pad** — clicks on the rest of the page are normal browser clicks and are not counted.
- **The side buttons** — back and forward are often wired to browser history outside this pad. Inside the pad they should count instead.
- **A hardware switch** — some mice have a DPI or button-lock switch. Check the underside.
- **Another device** — a graphics tablet or a trackpad can be the pointer the page is seeing. Unplug the extra device and try again.

#### Double-click feels like one click

Operating systems collapse two clicks into a double-click only when they land inside a time window and a small distance. This page uses 500 milliseconds, which is a common default. If your double-clicks show a gap well above that, slow the system double-click speed — or the switch is bouncing and needs a clean.

### FAQ

**Where does Mouse Tester run?**
Mouse Tester runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**How do I test the right mouse button?**
Right-click inside the grid pad. The browser’s menu is blocked there so the click can be counted. The Right counter should go up by one.

**What is a normal double-click speed?**
Anything up to about 500 milliseconds between the two clicks. The page shows the exact gap of the last double-click it accepted.

**Why does the page not scroll when I use the wheel?**
Wheel events over the pad are taken by the test so they can be counted. Move the pointer outside the pad to scroll the page again.

**Does it work with a trackpad?**
Yes. A click, a tap and a two-finger scroll are ordinary pointer and wheel events, so they show up the same way.

**Is the pointer position sent anywhere?**
No. Coordinates and counts stay in the tab. Reset clears them, and so does leaving the page.

## Dead Pixel Test

URL: https://justtools.info/device-tests/dead-pixel-test/
Category: Device Tests
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-22

Dead Pixel Test on Toolspire. Fill the screen with solid colours and a fine grid to spot dead, stuck or bright pixels. Nothing about your display is uploaded.

### At a glance

- Dead Pixel Test on Toolspire: fills the browser with **black, white, red, green, blue, cyan, magenta, yellow, gray** and a **fine grid**.
- Click, or the left and right arrow keys, moves to the next colour. **Escape** closes the test.
- A pixel that stays black on every colour is **dead**. A pixel that stays one colour is **stuck**. A pixel that is always bright is a **hot** pixel.
- The grid is an 8-pixel lattice on black, which makes one lit pixel stand out.
- The test is only colours on the page. It does not read the screen and does not upload a photo of it.

### Features

- **Solid primary colours**: Each subpixel — red, green and blue — gets a screen of its own, plus the mixes and black and white.
- **Full-screen layer**: The colour covers the site, including the header, so you can scan the whole panel.
- **A pixel grid**: The last screen draws a fine white grid. A stuck-on pixel shows up between the lines.
- **Keyboard or click**: Arrows and the space bar step through colours. Escape, or Close, leaves the test.

### How to look for a dead pixel

1. **Open the full-screen test** — Press **Open full screen**. Dim the room if the panel is glossy.
2. **Step through the colours** — Click the colour, or press the right arrow. Look for a dot that does not match the rest of the screen.
3. **Check black and white** — Dead pixels show on white and on bright colours. Stuck-on pixels show on black.
4. **Use the grid** — The grid screen is for a single bright pixel that is hard to see on a flat colour.

### Guide

#### Dead, stuck and hot

| What you see | What it usually is |
| --- | --- |
| Always black, on every colour | A dead pixel. The transistor is not lighting that dot. |
| Always red, green or blue | A stuck subpixel. One channel is on or off permanently. |
| Always bright, especially on black | A hot pixel. Common on camera sensors too, but on a monitor it is a stuck-on cell. |
| A smudge that moves when you press gently | Pressure on the panel, not a dead pixel. Stop pressing — panels bruise. |

#### The browser frame is still visible

Phones and some browsers will not let a page hide the address bar. Scroll that bar away, or rotate to landscape, then run the colours again. The dots you are hunting are on the panel, so a thin browser strip does not hide them.

### FAQ

**Where does Dead Pixel Test run?**
Dead Pixel Test runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**How do I test for dead pixels?**
Open the full-screen test and look at each solid colour from close up. A dot that stays black while the rest of the screen changes is dead.

**What is the difference between a dead and a stuck pixel?**
A dead pixel stays black. A stuck pixel stays lit in one colour — red, green, blue or white — no matter what the screen is showing.

**Can this test fix a dead pixel?**
No. It only helps you see one. A stuck pixel sometimes frees if the colour around it is flashed for a long time, but a dead pixel does not come back. Check the warranty before trying any “pixel massage”.

**Why is there a grid?**
On a flat black screen a single bright pixel is easy to miss. The grid gives the eye lines to follow so a dot between them stands out.

**Does the test photograph my screen?**
No. It only changes the page colour. It cannot see the panel, and it does not upload anything.

## Touch Screen Test

URL: https://justtools.info/device-tests/touch-screen-test/
Category: Device Tests
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-22

Touch Screen Test on Toolspire: Touch the corners and the centre, and see every finger the screen reports. Multi-touch stays in this tab and is not uploaded.

### At a glance

- Touch Screen Test on Toolspire: draws a dot for **every finger** the browser reports, and shows how many are down at once.
- Five targets — **four corners and the centre** — turn solid when a touch lands on them.
- With two fingers down, the page shows the **distance between them** in pixels.
- Remembers the **most fingers at once**, so you can see whether the screen’s multi-touch limit is 2, 5 or 10.
- Touch points stay in the tab. They are not stored and not uploaded. A mouse can click the targets on a computer.

### Features

- **Live fingers**: Each contact is a dot that follows your finger, including a second and a third.
- **Corner targets**: Dead zones often sit in the corners. The four circles plus the centre make those zones obvious.
- **Pinch distance**: Two fingers report how far apart they are, which is the raw input a pinch gesture uses.
- **A running maximum**: Lift and press again with more fingers. The “at once” number stays at the highest count.

### How to test a touch screen

1. **Open the page on the device** — A phone or tablet is the real test. A computer can still click the targets with a mouse.
2. **Hit the five circles** — Touch each corner and the centre. A circle that never turns solid is a dead zone.
3. **Put two fingers down** — You should see two dots and a pinch distance. Add fingers until the count stops rising — that is the screen’s limit.
4. **Drag along an edge** — A dot that jumps or vanishes as you slide is a scratch or a failing digitizer.

### Guide

#### A spot the finger cannot hit

- **A screen protector** — a lifted corner or a thick glass edge creates a dead band. Peel it back and try the same spot.
- **A case** — some cases cover the extreme edge. Take the case off before deciding the panel is faulty.
- **Water or oil** — dry the glass. A wet patch can spawn extra touches or swallow a real one.
- **The browser** — in-app browsers sometimes mishandle multi-touch. Open the page in Safari or Chrome and try again.

#### How many touches should a phone report?

Most phones sold in the last decade report at least five simultaneous touches, and many report ten. Two is enough for a pinch. If a modern phone never goes past one finger here, and it also fails in the Maps app, the digitizer — not the site — is the limit.

### FAQ

**Where does Touch Screen Test run?**
Touch Screen Test runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**How do I test multi-touch?**
Put two fingers on the stage at the same time. You should see two dots, a finger count of 2, and a pinch distance. Add fingers until the “at once” number stops increasing.

**Why do the corners matter?**
A failing touch layer often dies at the edges first. The four corner targets are there so a dead edge is obvious, not just a miss in the middle.

**Can I use this on a laptop touchpad?**
A touchpad is a pointing device, so it moves one pointer. It will not show ten fingers. Use a phone or tablet screen for the multi-touch count.

**The page scrolls instead of drawing a dot.**
The stage is set not to scroll while you touch it. If the whole page still moves, you are touching outside the box. Stay inside the bordered area.

**Are touches uploaded?**
No. Finger positions exist only while the page is open. Reset clears the targets, and closing the tab clears everything.

### Guide

#### Screen sizes included

Sizes are CSS viewports — what a media query measures — not the physical pixels of the display.

| Device | Viewport | Tailwind | Bootstrap |

| iPhone SE | 375 × 667 | base | xs |
