- **11 card sets**: animals, food, travel, nature, shapes and colours, numbers, letters — and learning sets that pair **A with a**, **3 + 4 with 7**, or **a picture with its word**, plus Hindi letters.
- Play **on your own** against the clock (with stars and your best scores), **against the computer** with a forgetful, good or sharp memory, or with **2 to 4 friends**.
- An optional **peek** shows every card for 3 seconds at the start — a gentle start for younger players.
- Memory (also called Concentration or Pairs) is a classic card game you can also play with an ordinary pack of cards. Free, no account.

### Features

- **Learning card sets**: Capital and small letters, sums and answers, pictures and words, numbers and Hindi letters.
- **You against the computer**: Its memory is forgetful, good or sharp — it remembers cards it has seen, just like you.
- **Pass and play**: Two to four players take turns; find a pair and you go again.
- **Stars and best scores**: Playing alone, you get up to three stars and your best turns and time for each grid.
- **Smooth flips**: Cards turn over in 3D, pairs glow, and the sound can be switched off.
- **Keyboard friendly**: Tab or the arrow keys move between cards; Enter or Space turns one over.

### How to play the memory game

1. **Choose your cards** — Pick a card set and a grid size — 6 pairs for little ones, 18 for experts.
2. **Turn over two cards** — Tap a card to see it, then tap another.
3. **Keep the pairs** — If they match, they stay face up and you go again.
4. **Remember the rest** — If they don’t match, they turn back over. Remember where they were for later.
5. **Clear the board** — The game ends when every pair is found. Alone, aim for fewer turns; with others, the most pairs wins.

### Guide

#### Grid sizes

| Grid | Cards | Good for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 6 pairs | 4 × 3 = 12 | Young children |
| 8 pairs | 4 × 4 = 16 | A quick game |
| 10 pairs | 5 × 4 = 20 | Older children |
| 15 pairs | 6 × 5 = 30 | Adults |
| 18 pairs | 6 × 6 = 36 | A real memory test |

#### Memory game tips

- **Work in order**: turn over cards row by row, so you remember positions more easily.
- **Say what you see** — “cat, top left” — saying it in your head helps you remember.
- **Turn a known card second**: if your first card matches one you have seen, go straight to it.
- **Learn something new**: when you turn an unknown card first and it doesn’t match anything you remember, use your second turn to uncover another new card.
- Playing alone, **three stars** means about one and a half turns per pair or fewer.

#### About the memory game

Memory — also known as Concentration, Pairs or Pelmanism — is played with cards laid face down. Players turn over two at a time looking for matches, so it rewards attention and short-term memory. It is a favourite with teachers because the same game can practise letters, numbers, sums and new words.

### FAQ

**Where does Memory Game run?**
Memory Game runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**How do you play the memory game?**
Turn over two cards. If they match, they stay up and you go again; if not, they turn back. Find all the pairs — alone in as few turns as possible, or more pairs than the other players.

**Is there a memory game for kids?**
Yes. Choose 6 or 8 pairs, a picture set such as **Animals**, and switch on **Show all cards for 3 seconds**. The learning sets practise letters, sums and reading.

**Can I play against the computer?**
Yes. Choose **Computer** and how good its memory is: forgetful, good or sharp.

**Can several people play?**
Yes — choose **Friends** for 2 to 4 players on one device. Finding a pair gives you another turn.

**How are the stars worked out?**
Three stars for about 1.5 turns per pair or fewer, two stars up to about 2.1 turns per pair, otherwise one star.

**Is it free?**
Yes, free with no account. Your settings and best scores stay in this browser.

## Jigsaw Puzzle

URL: https://justtools.info/games/jigsaw-puzzle/

Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.

Play jigsaw puzzles here: famous paintings like The Starry Night, or turn your own photo into a puzzle. 12 to 150 pieces that snap together.

### At a glance

- Jigsaw Puzzle on Toolspire: classic **jigsaw-shaped pieces** with tabs and blanks, cut differently every game. Drag them onto the board — matching pieces **snap together**.
- Choose **12, 24, 48, 96 or 150 pieces**: a quick puzzle for children or a long one for a quiet evening.
- **12 famous pictures**: Van Gogh’s The Starry Night, Hokusai’s Great Wave, Raja Ravi Varma, Monet, Klimt, Vermeer and NASA’s Blue Marble — all public domain.
- **Use your own photo**: it is cut into pieces in this tab and not sent to us.
- Helpers when you want them: **edges only**, a **faint picture** on the board, a look at the **finished picture**, **tidy** the pieces, a **hint**, and **full screen**.
- Your puzzle is **saved as you go**, so you can come back later. Free, no account.

### Features

- **Real jigsaw pieces**: Rounded tabs and blanks, a slight bevel and shadows — and a new cut every time.
- **Your own photo**: Turn a family photo or a holiday picture into a puzzle, privately on your device.
- **Famous paintings**: Public-domain masterpieces from Van Gogh to Raja Ravi Varma, plus the Earth from Apollo 17.
- **Snap together**: Pieces join when they line up and lock when they reach their place on the board.
- **Edges first**: Show only the edge pieces to build the frame, like on a real table.
- **Saved as you go**: Close the page and pick up exactly where you left off.

### How to do a jigsaw puzzle online

1. **Pick a picture** — Choose a painting, or tap **Your photo** to use a picture from your phone or computer.
2. **Choose the pieces** — Pick 12 to 150 pieces. The pieces are scattered around the board.
3. **Build the frame** — Press **Edges only** and put the straight-edged pieces together first.
4. **Fill it in** — Drag pieces near their neighbours; they snap together and move as one. Pieces lock when they reach their place.
5. **Finish** — When the last piece is in, the puzzle is solved and your time is saved.

### Guide

#### Piece counts

| Pieces | Good for | Typical time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 12 | Young children | A minute or two |
| 24 | Children | A few minutes |
| 48 | A coffee break | 10–20 minutes |
| 96 | Puzzle fans | 30 minutes or more |
| 150 | A long evening (best on a big screen) | An hour or more |

#### Jigsaw puzzle tips

- **Do the edges first** — straight-edged pieces make the frame and give you a guide.
- **Sort by colour**: drag the sky pieces to one side and the dark pieces to another.
- **Look at the shape**: a piece with two tabs opposite each other fits between two blanks.
- Stuck? **Show the picture** for a moment, or use a **hint** to place one piece.
- On a phone, choose 24 or 48 pieces, or turn the phone sideways and use **full screen**.

#### About the pictures

The built-in pictures are public-domain artworks from Wikimedia Commons: The Starry Night and Café Terrace at Night and Sunflowers by Vincent van Gogh, The Great Wave off Kanagawa by Katsushika Hokusai, Woman Holding a Fruit by Raja Ravi Varma, Water Lilies and Impression, Sunrise by Claude Monet, The Hunters in the Snow by Pieter Bruegel the Elder, The Kiss by Gustav Klimt, A Sunday on La Grande Jatte by Georges Seurat, Girl with a Pearl Earring by Johannes Vermeer, and The Blue Marble photographed by the crew of Apollo 17 (NASA).

The London mapmaker John Spilsbury is believed to have made the first jigsaw puzzle around 1760: a map mounted on wood and cut along the borders of countries, sold as a “dissected map” to teach geography.

**Can I make a jigsaw puzzle from my own photo?**
Yes. Tap **Your photo** and choose a picture. It is cut into pieces right in this tab — the photo is not uploaded anywhere.

**How many pieces can I choose?**
12, 24, 48, 96 or 150. The exact number depends a little on the picture’s shape, so pieces stay close to square.

**How do pieces snap together?**
Drop a piece close to a neighbour in the right position and they join; groups move together. A piece or group dropped near its place on the board locks in.

**Is my puzzle saved?**
Yes, after every move, in this browser. Close the page and it will be waiting for you.

**Does it work on a phone or tablet?**
Yes — drag pieces with your finger. For more room, turn the screen sideways and tap **Full screen**.

**Are the pictures free to use?**
Yes. All the built-in pictures are in the public domain.

## Step-up SIP Calculator

URL: https://justtools.info/calculators/step-up-sip-calculator/
Category: Calculators
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-23

Project a monthly SIP that increases by a fixed percent each year, and separate the money you deposit from the gain. Open Step-up SIP Calculator on Toolspire.

### At a glance

- Step-up SIP Calculator on Toolspire: the monthly amount is constant for **12 instalments**, then multiplied by (1 + step ÷ 100).
- A **10% step** on ₹5,000 becomes ₹5,500 in year two and ₹6,050 in year three.
- Each month the new instalment is added and the balance then grows by **annual return ÷ 12**.
- At **0% step and 0% return**, one year of ₹1,000 a month is exactly ₹12,000.

### Features

- **Anniversary step**: The SIP rises once a year, which is how most fund houses schedule an increase.
- **Deposit versus gain**: See what you paid in and what growth added.
- **Flat-SIP check**: Set the step to 0 to compare with an ordinary SIP.

### How to project a step-up SIP

1. **Start with year one** — Type the monthly amount you can invest now, not the amount you hope to reach later.
2. **Set the yearly step** — 10 means the instalment rises 10% after every twelve months.
3. **Test more than one return** — Run 8%, 10% and 12%. The gap between them is the uncertainty, not a forecast.

### Guide

#### When the instalment changes

Twelve deposits use the same amount. On the next anniversary the amount is multiplied by (1 + step ÷ 100). Interest is a monthly estimate of NAV growth, not the exact units a fund would allot.

### FAQ

**Where does Step-up SIP Calculator run?**
Step-up SIP Calculator runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**What is a step-up SIP?**
A monthly mutual-fund investment that increases once a year, usually by a percent, so the instalment grows with income.

**How is the final corpus worked out?**
Each month the SIP is added and the balance grows by the annual return divided by 12. After 12 months the SIP amount itself steps up.

**Does zero step match a normal SIP?**
Yes. ₹1,000 a month for a year at 0% return finishes at ₹12,000, which is the ordinary SIP with no growth.

**Is this return guaranteed?**
No. The rate is a what-if. Real NAVs move, and tax can apply when you sell.

## Lumpsum Calculator

URL: https://justtools.info/calculators/lumpsum-calculator/
Category: Calculators
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-23

Lumpsum Calculator on Toolspire. See what a one-time investment can become after yearly compounding, and how much of the result is growth rather than principal.

### At a glance

- Lumpsum Calculator on Toolspire: future value uses **yearly compounding**: amount × (1 + rate) ^ years.
- The detail line splits **principal** and **gain**.
- A ₹1,00,000 lumpsum at 0% for any term stays ₹1,00,000.
- Use it to compare a bonus invested today with a SIP started beside it.

### Features

- **Shows the working**: Future value uses yearly compounding: amount × (1 + rate) ^ years.
- **Editable assumptions**: Rates and years are inputs, so you can test a cautious case and an optimistic one.
- **Private**: The numbers stay in this tab. Nothing is sent to a server.

### How to use this calculator

1. **Enter the amounts** — Use the same currency for every money field. Do not mix monthly and yearly by accident.
2. **Set the rate you want to test** — A past average is not a promise. Run the number twice with a lower rate.
3. **Read the detail line** — The large figure is the headline. The sentence under it is what went into it.

### Guide

#### What the number does and does not mean

Because the full amount is invested immediately, a lumpsum beats a SIP of the same total money if the market rises steadily. It loses if the market falls just after you invest. The calculator cannot know which path you will get; it only applies the rate you type.

### FAQ

**Where does Lumpsum Calculator run?**
Lumpsum Calculator runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**What is a lumpsum investment?**
A single amount invested once, rather than a monthly SIP. The whole principal starts compounding on day one.

**What formula is used?**
Future value = amount × (1 + rate ÷ 100) ^ years. A 12% rate for 10 years multiplies the amount by about 3.11.

**How is this different from a SIP calculator?**
A SIP adds money every month, so later instalments earn for less time. A lumpsum earns on the full amount for the whole term.

**Does this deduct tax or fund expenses?**
No. Expense ratios and capital-gains tax would make the take-home amount smaller.

## XIRR Calculator

URL: https://justtools.info/calculators/xirr-calculator/
Category: Calculators
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-23

XIRR Calculator on Toolspire. Work out the annualised return of irregular investments and payouts. This is the XIRR figure mutual-fund apps show for a SIP.

### At a glance

- XIRR Calculator on Toolspire: **XIRR** is the annual rate that sets the present value of every dated cash flow to zero.
- Investments are **negative**. Redemptions and the current value are **positive**.
- ₹1,000 invested and ₹1,100 returned exactly one year later is about **10% XIRR**.
- The year count is actual days divided by 365, so a SIP instalment from June is not treated as a full year.

### Features

- **Uneven dates**: Extra purchases and a partial sale can sit on any day.
- **SIP-style result**: This is the annualised number fund apps label XIRR, not a simple point-to-point CAGR.
- **Fails honestly**: If every amount has the same sign, the page refuses instead of inventing a rate.

### How to calculate XIRR

1. **List purchases as negatives** — Each line is a date, a comma, and the amount. A buy of 10,000 on 1 Jan 2025 is 2025-01-01, -10000.
2. **Add money that came back** — Dividends and sales are positive. So is the value of units you still hold, dated today.
3. **Read the annual rate** — 10% a year means the dated flows behave like a 10% compound return, not that every rupee earned 10%.

### Guide

#### XIRR is not CAGR

CAGR uses one start value, one end value and one time span. A SIP has many start dates. XIRR gives each instalment credit only for the days it was actually invested, which is why a fund that “returned 12% CAGR” on its NAV can show a lower XIRR on your SIP.

### FAQ

**Where does XIRR Calculator run?**
XIRR Calculator runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**What is XIRR?**
The annualised return for cash flows that are not evenly spaced. It is the right figure for a SIP, a staggered stock purchase, or a private investment with odd dates.

**Why are my investments entered as negative?**
The formula treats cash you pay as an outflow. Cash you could withdraw is an inflow. Mixing up the signs produces a nonsense rate.

**Which date do I use for units I still hold?**
Today’s date, and the amount you would receive if you redeemed at the latest NAV. Leaving that value out ignores the investment that is still working.

**Can two flows on the same day be combined?**
Yes. Add the amounts if they share a date, or keep them on separate lines. The rate uses the date, not the number of lines.

Flat vs Reducing Calculator on Toolspire. Compare a flat-rate EMI with a reducing-balance EMI on the same principal, annual rate and tenure.

### At a glance

- Flat vs Reducing Calculator on Toolspire: flat interest is **principal × annual rate × years**, spread evenly across the months.
- The reducing EMI is the standard loan formula on the **outstanding balance**.
- At **0%** both EMIs equal principal ÷ months, so you can see the page is comparing like with like.
- The headline shows the **reducing EMI**. The detail line has the flat EMI and both totals.

### Features

- **Same nominal rate, different cost**: Ten percent flat costs more than ten percent reducing because the full principal stays in the interest sum.
- **Totals, not just the EMI**: A smaller EMI can still be the dearer loan. Compare the two totals in the detail.
- **Zero-rate check**: With no interest, both methods return the principal split by the number of months.

### How to use the Flat vs Reducing Calculator

1. **Use the rate written on the quote** — Do not convert a flat rate into a reducing rate yourself before typing. This page does that comparison.
2. **Keep tenure in years** — A 36-month loan is 3 years. The page rounds years to the nearest month count.
3. **Compare the totals** — The reducing EMI is the big number. The sentence under it is where the flat quote shows its real cost.

### Guide

#### What the number is actually counting

Flat interest ignores repayments: the lender multiplies the opening principal by the annual rate and by the years, then divides principal plus that interest by the number of months. Reducing interest recalculates each month on the balance left. A flat quote at 10% is a different product from a reducing quote at 10%.

### FAQ

Interest is computed on the original principal for every year, even after you have repaid part of it. The reducing method shrinks that base.

Ask for the reducing-balance rate, then compare total money paid. A low flat rate can still cost more.

**Is the headline the flat EMI?**
No. The large figure is the reducing-balance EMI. The flat EMI is in the detail so the two totals sit together.

**Does this include processing fees?**
No. Add fees and insurance yourself. They are not part of either interest method.

Yes. The headline is the exclusive amount plus VAT. The amount you typed is the net.

## Percentage Change Calculator

URL: https://justtools.info/calculators/percentage-change-calculator/
Category: Calculators
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-23

Measure the percent rise or fall from an old number to a new number, using (new − old) ÷ old. The maths stays on your device.

### At a glance

- Percentage Change Calculator on Toolspire: the change is **(new − old) ÷ old × 100**. The sign is positive for a rise and negative for a fall.
- A move from **80 to 100 is +25%**. The reverse, 100 to 80, is −20%, because the base is now 100.
- A starting value of **0** has no percentage change. The page returns no result instead of infinity.
- This is one jump between two numbers. It is **not CAGR**, which spreads a change across years.

### Features

- **The base is the old number**: Percent change always divides by where you started, not by the new number and not by the average.
- **Direction in words**: The detail says increase, decrease, or no change, so a minus sign is not the only clue.
- **Two decimal places**: The percent is rounded to the nearest 0.01 so 1/3 of a percent does not spill digits.

### How to use the Percentage Change Calculator

1. **Put the earlier number first** — Old value is the base. If you swap the boxes, you answer a different question.
2. **Keep the units the same** — Do not compare rupees with thousands. 1500 to 1800 is the same percent as 1.5 to 1.8 only if both are in the same scale.
3. **Use CAGR for a multi-year price** — A share that went from 100 to 200 in five years did not “change by 100% a year”. Open the CAGR calculator for the annualised rate.

### Guide

#### What the number is actually counting

Percentage change answers “how large was this jump compared with the start?”. Percentage difference, which divides by the average of the two numbers, is a different statistic and is not what this page computes. A zero base is undefined, so it is rejected.

### FAQ

**Where does Percentage Change Calculator run?**
Percentage Change Calculator runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**Is percentage change the same as percentage difference?**
No. Change divides by the old value. Difference usually divides by the average of the two values. This page is the change formula.

**Why is +25% down to the start not −25%?**
Because the base changed. Falling from 100 to 80 divides a drop of 20 by 100, which is 20%, not 25%.

**What if the old value is negative?**
The formula still runs. Read the sign carefully: the base is negative, so the words “increase” and “decrease” follow the arithmetic, which can feel backwards in plain speech.

**How is this different from the percentage calculator?**
That tool finds a percent of a number, or a number from a percent. This tool only compares an old value with a new one.

## LCM and HCF Calculator

URL: https://justtools.info/education-tools/lcm-hcf-calculator/
Category: Education Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-23

LCM and HCF Calculator on Toolspire: Find the HCF and LCM of two integers with Euclid’s algorithm. LCM is the product divided by the HCF.

### At a glance

- LCM and HCF Calculator on Toolspire: HCF is the **Euclidean algorithm**: replace the larger number by the remainder until the remainder is 0.
- LCM is **|a| ÷ HCF × |b|**, which avoids multiplying the two numbers first and overflowing the school-sized product.
- **12 and 18** give HCF 6 and LCM 36. That pair is the check on the page.
- Decimals and **zero** are rejected. HCF and LCM in this school sense are for non-zero integers.

### Features

- **Remainder loop, not a factor list**: Euclid does not list every divisor. It only keeps replacing a with b and b with a mod b.
- **LCM from the HCF**: Once the HCF is known, the LCM is fixed. The page does not search multiples.
- **Signs ignored for the size**: The factors use absolute values. −12 and 18 still report HCF 6 and LCM 36.

### How to use the LCM and HCF Calculator

1. **Type whole numbers** — 12.5 is not accepted. If a textbook problem has decimals, scale both numbers to integers first and say so in your working.
2. **Read HCF as the headline** — The large result is the highest common factor. The LCM is the sentence underneath.
3. **Check with the product** — For positive integers, HCF × LCM equals the product of the two numbers. 6 × 36 = 12 × 18.

### Guide

#### Why the LCM uses the HCF

Searching multiples is slow and easy to stop too early. Euclid’s loop finds the greatest common divisor with remainders, and the identity LCM(a, b) = |a × b| / HCF(a, b) then gives the least common multiple. Dividing before multiplying keeps the intermediate value smaller. The page stops at two numbers; three numbers need a second pass of the same idea.

### FAQ

**Where does LCM and HCF Calculator run?**
LCM and HCF Calculator runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**What is the difference between HCF and GCD?**
They are the same function. HCF is the school name in India; GCD is the name in most programming libraries. Both mean the greatest positive integer that divides both numbers.

**Can I enter three numbers?**
Not on this page. Find the HCF of the first pair, then the HCF of that result and the third number. The LCM chains the same way.

**Why is zero rejected?**
Every non-zero integer divides 0, so the HCF is just the other number, and the LCM is 0 in some definitions. School questions do not use that case, so the page asks for a non-zero integer.

**Does order matter?**
No. HCF(18, 12) equals HCF(12, 18), and the LCM matches too.

## Prime Factorization

URL: https://justtools.info/education-tools/prime-factorization/
Category: Education Tools

Prime Factorization on Toolspire: Split an integer from 2 up to one trillion into prime factors by trial division, and say so when the number itself is prime.

### At a glance

- Prime Factorization on Toolspire: trial division strips **factors of 2**, then odd primes up to the square root of what remains.
- **84** factors as **2 × 2 × 3 × 7**. A prime such as 17 is returned as itself with the word prime.
- The input must be an integer from **2 to 1,000,000,000,000**. 1 is not a prime and is not factored.
- Repeats stay written out. **12** is 2 × 2 × 3, so the exponents are visible as copies.

### Features

- **Odd candidates only after 2**: Once twos are removed, the loop steps by 2, so it never tests an even divisor again.
- **Stops at the square root**: If a factor larger than the square root existed, its pair would already have been found.
- **Prime called out**: A single-factor result is labelled prime instead of looking like a failed tree.

### How to use the Prime Factorization

1. **Start from an integer greater than 1** — 1, 0 and negatives are not factored. Decimals are rejected.
2. **Multiply the factors back** — The product of the numbers in the headline should equal the integer you typed.
3. **Use the factors for HCF by hand** — Shared primes, taking the smaller power, are the HCF. The LCM page does that without a factor list.

### Guide

#### What trial division skips

After the factors of two are gone, only odd divisors are tested, and only while the square of the candidate is still at most the remaining value. A remaining value above 1 at the end is itself prime. This is the classroom method, not a sieve, so a 12-digit prime can take a moment. Numbers above one trillion are refused so the loop stays bounded.

### FAQ

**Where does Prime Factorization run?**
Prime Factorization runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**Is 1 a prime number?**
No. This page rejects 1. Prime factorization is defined for integers greater than 1.

**Why are repeated primes written twice?**
So the line multiplies back to the original number without you having to expand exponents. 2 × 2 × 3 is 12.

**Can this factor a very large prime?**
Up to one trillion. Past that the page refuses rather than running a long trial loop in the tab.

**How do I use this to find an HCF?**
Factor both numbers and keep the primes they share, with the lower power. For a direct answer, the LCM and HCF calculator is shorter.

## Factorial Calculator

URL: https://justtools.info/education-tools/factorial-calculator/
Category: Education Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-23

Factorial Calculator on Toolspire. Calculate n factorial as an exact integer with BigInt, from 0! = 1 through 500!, and show how many digits the result has.

### At a glance

- Factorial Calculator on Toolspire: n! is **1 × 2 × … × n**, computed with **BigInt** so 20! is exact, not a rounded float.
- **0! is 1** by the empty-product convention. That value is what makes nPr formulas work when r = n.
- The page accepts integers from **0 to 500**. 10! is 3,628,800.
- The detail line is the **digit count** of the full integer, which is the useful check once the number no longer fits on one glance.

### Features

- **Exact digits**: Floating point cannot hold 25! exactly. BigInt keeps every digit.
- **A published ceiling**: 500! is allowed. 501 is refused so a pasted accident does not lock the tab.
- **Digit count beside the integer**: You can check a large factorial by its length even when you do not re-multiply every step.

### How to use the Factorial Calculator

1. **Type a whole n** — Decimals are rejected. Factorial is not defined for 4.5 on this page; that would be a gamma function.
2. **Start from a known value** — Try 5 and confirm 120, or 0 and confirm 1, before you trust a large result.
3. **Copy the full integer** — The headline is the entire factorial. The copy button takes that string, not the digit count.

### Guide

#### Why 0! is 1 here

The product of no numbers is defined as 1 so that n! = n × (n−1)! still holds when n is 1. Permutations use that fact: the number of ways to arrange n items out of n is n! / 0! = n!. This calculator follows that convention. It does not compute the gamma function for fractional n, and it does not switch to scientific notation.

### FAQ

**Where does Factorial Calculator run?**
Factorial Calculator runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**What is 0 factorial?**
1. The page returns that on purpose. It is the value used in permutation formulas when you arrange every item.

**How far can n go?**
500. Above that the page returns no result. The integer would be enormous and slow to build in a tab.

**Why is 20! not written with an e?**
Because it is exact. A floating-point factorial would round. BigInt keeps the digits.

**Is factorial defined for negatives?**
Not in this school definition. Negative n is rejected.

## Permutation Combination Calculator

URL: https://justtools.info/education-tools/permutation-combination-calculator/
Category: Education Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-23

Permutation Combination Calculator on Toolspire: Calculate nPr and nCr with exact integers. Order counts for permutations and does not count for combinations.

### At a glance

- Permutation Combination Calculator on Toolspire: **nPr = n! / (n − r)!**. It counts arrangements, so order matters.
- **nCr = nPr / r!**. It counts groups, so {A, B} and {B, A} are one combination.
- **5P2 = 20** and **5C2 = 10**. Those are the checks built into the test.
- n and r must be integers, **r cannot exceed n**, and n stops at **500** so the factorials stay bounded.

### Features

- **Both counts on one page**: The headline is nPr. The detail is nCr. You can see that combinations are the permutations divided by r!.
- **Exact division**: BigInt factorials divide evenly for these formulas, so 5C2 is 10 and not 9.999.
- **Refuses r greater than n**: Choosing 6 items from 5 is not given a zero disguised as a result. It is rejected.

### How to use the Permutation Combination Calculator

1. **Decide whether order matters** — A podium (gold, silver, bronze) is a permutation. A committee of three, with no roles, is a combination.
2. **Type n first and r second** — n is the size of the pool. r is how many you pick. Swapping them usually makes the page reject the input.
3. **Check 5 and 2** — You should see nPr 20 and nCr 10 before you use the page on a larger class list.

### Guide

#### When to divide by r!

Each combination of r items can be arranged in r! orders. Counting arrangements first (nPr) and then dividing by r! removes those orders and leaves the combination. If the question says “arrange”, “rank” or “password”, keep nPr. If it says “choose”, “committee” or “hand of cards”, use nCr. The page shows both so the extra division is visible.

### FAQ

**Where does Permutation Combination Calculator run?**
Permutation Combination Calculator runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**What is the difference between nPr and nCr?**
nPr counts ordered selections. nCr counts unordered ones. nCr is nPr divided by r factorial.

**What is 5C2?**
10. The pairs from five items are ten, because order inside a pair is not a new pair.

**Why is nCn equal to 1?**
There is one way to choose every item. nPn is n!, the arrangements of all of them. The page shows both.

**Can r be zero?**
Yes. There is one way to choose nothing, and one way to arrange nothing, so both results are 1.

## Mean Median Mode Calculator

URL: https://justtools.info/education-tools/mean-median-mode-calculator/
Category: Education Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-23

Mean Median Mode Calculator on Toolspire: Find the mean, median and mode of a list of numbers. The mode is reported only when a value actually repeats.

### At a glance

- Mean Median Mode Calculator on Toolspire: the mean is the **arithmetic average**: the sum divided by how many numbers were parsed.
- The median is the **middle of the sorted list**. An even count uses the average of the two middle numbers.
- The mode is every value that appears **most often**, and only if it appears more than once. A list of unique numbers has no mode.
- **1, 2, 2, 9** has mean 3.5, median 2 and mode 2.

### Features

- **All three on one paste**: You do not pick a mode. Mean, median and mode are computed from the same tokens.
- **No fake mode**: If every value appears once, the detail says there is no mode instead of listing the whole set.
- **Two middle values**: An even-sized list does not pick the lower middle only. It averages the two central numbers.

### How to use the Mean Median Mode Calculator

1. **Paste the raw list** — Commas, spaces and line breaks all work. Words are ignored; only number tokens are read.
2. **Sort in your head for the median** — The page sorts a copy. Your original order does not change the median.
3. **Treat “no mode” as an answer** — If nothing repeats, say there is no mode. Do not invent one by picking the first number.

### Guide

#### Which average a list is asking for

The mean moves when a single outlier moves. The median does not, as long as the outlier stays on the same side of the middle. The mode is about the most common value, and a list can have more than one. School questions that say “find the three averages” want all of these from the same data, which is why they share a page instead of hiding inside the plain average tool.

### FAQ

**Where does Mean Median Mode Calculator run?**
Mean Median Mode Calculator runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**Can a list have two modes?**
Yes. If two values tie for the highest frequency, both are listed. A list where everything appears once has no mode.

**How is the median of an even list found?**
Sort the list and average the two central numbers. For 1, 2, 2, 9 the two central numbers are both 2, so the median is 2.

**Does the average calculator already do this?**
The average tool is the mean. This page adds the median and the mode, which that tool does not report.

**Are negative numbers allowed?**
Yes. A leading minus is part of the number. The mean can be negative.

## Standard Deviation Calculator

URL: https://justtools.info/education-tools/standard-deviation-calculator/
Category: Education Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-23

Standard Deviation Calculator on Toolspire. Calculate the sample and population standard deviation of a list. No account is required.

### At a glance

- Standard Deviation Calculator on Toolspire: both figures use the **squared distance from the mean**. They differ only in the divisor.
- The sample standard deviation divides by **n − 1**. The population figure divides by **n**.
- For **1, 2, 3** the sample standard deviation is **1** and the population figure is **√(2/3)**, about 0.8165.
- Fewer than **two numbers** is rejected. A single observation has no sample spread.

### Features

- **Sample is the headline**: Most pasted marks are a sample. The n − 1 divisor is the number in large type.
- **Population sits beside it**: If your list is the entire class, not a sample, use the population figure in the detail.
- **The mean is shown too**: You can see the centre the gaps were measured from, without opening the average page.

### How to use the Standard Deviation Calculator

1. **Paste every observation** — Leave out blanks. A double comma does not insert a zero; only real number tokens count.
2. **Pick the divisor your question names** — If the question says “sample” or does not say the list is complete, use the headline. If it says “population” or “entire data”, use the detail.
3. **Check 1, 2, 3** — Sample standard deviation 1 is the easy confirmation that n − 1 was used.

### Guide

#### Why the two divisors disagree

Dividing the sum of squared gaps by n understates the spread when those observations are a sample from a larger population. The n − 1 divisor, Bessel’s correction, is the usual fix, and it is what spreadsheets call STDEV.S. STDEV.P divides by n. This page prints both and names them, so a homework question that says “population” is not answered with the sample formula by accident.

### FAQ

**Where does Standard Deviation Calculator run?**
Standard Deviation Calculator runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**Which standard deviation is the headline?**
The sample one, dividing by n − 1. The population value, dividing by n, is in the detail and labelled.

**What is the standard deviation of 1, 2 and 3?**
The sample value is 1. The population value is the square root of 2/3, about 0.8165.

**Why do I need two numbers?**
With one number the gaps are zero and the sample divisor is zero. The page asks for a second observation.

**Is this variance?**
No. Variance is the average squared gap before the square root. The figures here are standard deviations, the square roots of those variances.

## Final Grade Calculator

URL: https://justtools.info/education-tools/final-grade-calculator/
Category: Education Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-23

Final Grade Calculator on Toolspire: Find the score you still need on the remaining weight of a course to finish at a target percentage.

### At a glance

- Final Grade Calculator on Toolspire: needed score = **(target − current × completed share) ÷ remaining share**.
- The completed share is **100% minus the weight you still have left**. A final worth 40% means 60% is already graded.
- **80% so far, 40% left, target 70%** needs **55%** on what remains.
- A result **above 100** means the target is out of reach. A result **below 0** means you already cleared it even with a zero.

### Features

- **Weight is the unmarked share**: Type 40 if the final is 40% of the course. Do not type the points on the exam paper unless those points are the percent.
- **Impossible targets stay visible**: 105% is shown, with a line that says the target is out of reach, instead of being clipped to 100.
- **Already safe is visible too**: A negative needed score is kept and explained: a zero on the rest still meets the target.

### How to use the Final Grade Calculator

1. **Confirm the current grade is a percent** — If the portal says 80 / 100, type 80. If it says 320 / 400, convert to a percent first.
2. **Type only the weight that is left** — Add the final and any unmarked homework if both are still open, and type that combined percent.
3. **Read above-100 as a no** — You cannot score 110% on a normal paper. Lower the target or accept the grade the arithmetic allows.

### Guide

#### The completed share is implied

The formula assumes the current grade already averages everything that has been marked, and that the weight you type is the only part left. It does not know about extra credit, dropped tests or a curve. If the syllabus weights do not add to 100, fix that before you type. A needed score over 100 is an honest result: the target cannot be reached on the remaining weight.

### FAQ

**Where does Final Grade Calculator run?**
Final Grade Calculator runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**What does the weight box mean?**
The percent of the course that is not in your current grade yet. A final worth 40% of the course is 40, even if the paper has 80 marks.

**What if I need more than 100%?**
The target is impossible with that weight. The page still shows the figure so you can see how far short the goal is.

**What if the result is negative?**
You already meet the target even if the remaining work scores zero. The detail says so.

**How is this different from a weighted grade?**
Weighted grade averages scores you already have. This page solves for the score you do not have yet.

## Weighted Grade Calculator

URL: https://justtools.info/education-tools/weighted-grade-calculator/
Category: Education Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-23

Weighted Grade Calculator on Toolspire. Average graded rows where each line is a score and a weight. The result is the weight-adjusted percent.

### At a glance

- Weighted Grade Calculator on Toolspire: each line is **score × weight**. The grade is the sum of those products divided by the **sum of the weights**.
- Weights can be percents or any relative size. **80 with weight 1 and 90 with weight 3** is **87.5%**.
- A weight of **zero** adds nothing. A negative weight is rejected.
- This averages marks you **already have**. It does not solve for a future final. That is the final-grade page.

### Features

- **One assessment per line**: Score first, weight second, separated by a comma or a space.
- **Relative weights**: Weights of 1 and 3 behave like 25% and 75%. You do not have to make them add to 100.
- **The weight total is shown**: The detail reports the sum of the weights so a missing row is easier to spot.

### How to use the Weighted Grade Calculator

1. **Put the score before the weight** — 80, 1 means a score of 80 with weight 1. Swapping the columns changes the grade.
2. **Use the syllabus weights** — If quizzes are 20% and the midterm is 30%, those percents are valid weights. So are 2 and 3.
3. **Check 80 and 90** — The sample lines should read 87.5%. If they do not, a column is reversed.

### Guide

#### Weights do not need to sum to 100

Dividing by the total weight normalises the rows. A quiz weight of 1 and a final weight of 3 is the same average as weights 25 and 75. What matters is the ratio. A plain mean of the scores would treat the quiz as equal to the final, which is the mistake this page exists to avoid. Unmarked work does not belong in the list; use the final-grade calculator to solve for a score you do not have yet.

### FAQ

**Where does Weighted Grade Calculator run?**
Weighted Grade Calculator runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**Do the weights have to add up to 100?**
No. They are relative. 1 and 3 give the same result as 25 and 75.

**What goes on each line?**
The score, then the weight. 90, 3 is a score of 90 with weight 3.

**How do I include a test I have not taken?**
Leave it out. This page only averages rows you type. The final-grade calculator solves for a missing score.

**What is the sample answer?**
80 at weight 1 and 90 at weight 3 is (80 + 270) / 4 = 87.5%.

## Heron's Formula Calculator

URL: https://justtools.info/education-tools/herons-formula-calculator/
Category: Education Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-23

Heron's Formula Calculator on Toolspire: Find a triangle’s area from all three sides with Heron’s formula. No account is required.

### At a glance

- Heron's Formula Calculator on Toolspire: the semi-perimeter **s = (a + b + c) / 2**. Area = **√[s(s − a)(s − b)(s − c)]**.
- A **3-4-5** triangle has area **6**. That is the right-triangle check, without using the right angle.
- Sides that break the **triangle inequality** are rejected. 1, 2 and 10 do not form a triangle.
- The unit of the area is the **square of whatever unit the sides used**. The page does not convert centimetres to metres.

### Features

- **Three sides, no angle**: If you know the height instead, this is the wrong formula. Heron does not ask for a height.
- **Impossible triangles stop**: The page returns nothing when one side is longer than the other two combined.
- **Semi-perimeter in the detail**: You can recompute the product under the square root from s without guessing which step failed.

### How to use the Heron's Formula Calculator

1. **Use the same unit on every side** — Do not mix inches and centimetres. The area comes back in that unit squared.
2. **Try 3, 4 and 5** — The area should be 6. If it is not, the side boxes are not all filled.
3. **Stop if the page refuses** — A refusal means the lengths cannot meet. Measure again before you look for a rounding error.

### Guide

#### Heron does not need the height

The usual school area is base times height over two. Heron replaces the height with a combination of all three sides, which is what you have when you measured a plot and did not drop a perpendicular. The square root is zero when the points are colinear, and it is not real when the triangle inequality fails. Those inputs are rejected rather than shown as zero area.

### FAQ

**Where does Heron's Formula Calculator run?**
Heron's Formula Calculator runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**What is Heron’s formula?**
Area = √[s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)], where s is half the perimeter. It needs all three sides and no angle.

**What is the area of a 3-4-5 triangle?**
6 square units. It is also a right triangle, and (3 × 4) / 2 gives the same 6.

**Why did my sides get rejected?**
One side is at least as long as the other two put together, so the ends cannot meet.

**Can I use this for a right triangle?**
Yes. You do not need to tell the page about the right angle. Pythagoras is available when you only know two sides of a right triangle.

## Cylinder Volume Calculator

URL: https://justtools.info/education-tools/cylinder-volume-calculator/
Category: Education Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-23

Calculate the volume of a right circular cylinder and its total surface area from radius and height. The maths stays on your device.

### At a glance

- Cylinder Volume Calculator on Toolspire: volume = **π × radius² × height**. A radius of 1 and a height of 1 give **π**, about 3.1416.
- Total surface area = **2 π r (h + r)**, which is the lateral area plus two bases.
- A unit cylinder has surface area **4π**, about 12.5664. That is the second check.
- Radius and height must be **zero or positive** and in the **same unit**. The page does not ask for a diameter.

### Features

- **Volume is the headline**: The search is usually for capacity. Surface area is the second figure, labelled.
- **Both ends included**: Total surface is not the lateral area alone. The detail says two bases plus the side.
- **Radius, not diameter**: If you measured across the tin, halve it before typing. Diameter in the radius box doubles the volume fourfold.

### How to use the Cylinder Volume Calculator

1. **Halve the diameter** — A tin that is 10 cm across has radius 5. The page will not divide for you.
2. **Match the units** — Radius in centimetres and height in metres produces a nonsense volume. Convert first.
3. **Read the surface only if you are painting or wrapping** — The volume is the capacity. The surface is the material for the outside, including the top and bottom.

### Guide

#### Capacity and metal are different questions

Volume answers how much the cylinder holds. Total surface area answers how much material covers it, top and bottom included. Lateral area alone would drop the 2 π r² of the ends; this page does not drop them. π is the JavaScript value, and the display rounds to four decimal places. A cone or a hollow pipe needs a different formula.

### FAQ

**Where does Cylinder Volume Calculator run?**
Cylinder Volume Calculator runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**What is the volume of a cylinder?**
π times radius squared times height. Radius 1 and height 1 give π, shown as 3.1416.

**Does the surface area include the top and bottom?**
Yes. The formula used is 2 π r (h + r), lateral area plus two circles.

**What if I have the diameter?**
Divide it by two and type the radius. The page does not have a diameter box.

**Can the height be zero?**
Yes. The volume is zero and the surface is the two faces pressed together, 2 π r².

A perfect square in this school sense is an integer that is some integer times itself. 144 qualifies. 2 does not, even though it has a real square root. - The names are English weekdays, **Sunday through Saturday**, matching `Date`’s UTC day index.

#### Why the zone is fixed

JavaScript’s local date can turn a UTC midnight into the previous evening in the Americas. Naming weekdays from the local zone would make “what day was 1 January?” depend on the reader. This page builds the date with Date.UTC and reads getUTCDay, then checks the year, month and day still match. Historical calendar reforms before the Gregorian calendar are not applied.

Monday. The page uses that date as its check.

No. The weekday is computed in UTC so two people do not get two days for the same written date.

**What about 31 February?**
It is rejected. The page does not silently move it to 2 or 3 March.

**Can this count the days between two dates?**
No. It names one date. The date-difference calculator counts the span.

## ISO Week Number

URL: https://justtools.info/calculators/iso-week-number/
Category: Calculators
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-23

Find the ISO-8601 week number of a date, including the ISO year when the week belongs to the year next door. The maths stays on your device.

### At a glance

- ISO Week Number on Toolspire: the ISO week starts on **Monday**. Week 1 is the week with the year’s **first Thursday**, which is also the week that contains 4 January.
- **1 January 2021** is a Friday and belongs to **ISO week 53 of 2020**, not week 1 of 2021.
- The headline is the week number. The detail is the **ISO year**, which can be the previous or next calendar year.
- The date is read in **UTC** and checked the same way as the weekday tool, so 31 February is refused.

### Features

- **ISO year beside the week**: A week number without its ISO year is ambiguous in the first and last days of December and January.
- **Thursday rule**: The date is shifted to the Thursday of its week, and that Thursday’s year is the ISO year.
- **Not a US week**: Weeks here do not start on Sunday, and week 1 is not simply the week of 1 January.

### How to use the ISO Week Number

1. **Use the written date** — The week is a property of the calendar date, not of the hour. Leave the time off.
2. **Read the year in the detail** — If you only copy the week number in early January, you may be quoting the previous ISO year.
3. **Check 1 January 2021** — The page should say week 53 and ISO year 2020.

### Guide

#### Why 1 January is not always week 1

ISO-8601 wants every week to have seven days and to start on Monday. That forces a few days of late December or early January into the neighbouring year. The practical test is the Thursday: whichever year owns the Thursday owns the week. This page moves the date to that Thursday, then counts weeks from 1 January of that year. It does not follow the “week of 1 January” rule some payroll calendars still use.

### FAQ

**Where does ISO Week Number run?**
ISO Week Number runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**What ISO week is 1 January 2021?**
Week 53 of ISO year 2020. The Friday sits in the week whose Thursday was 31 December 2020.

**When does week 1 start?**
On the Monday of the week that contains the first Thursday of the calendar year. That Monday can fall in December.

**Is this the same as a US calendar week?**
No. Many US calendars start the week on Sunday and call the partial first week week 1. ISO does neither.

**Can the ISO year differ from the date’s year?**
Yes. That is why the detail prints the ISO year separately from the week number.

No. Twenty-five hours stays 25 hours. This page does not convert a duration into a time of day.

Convert 24-hour military time such as 14:30 into 2:30 PM, and show the 24-hour form back again. The maths stays on your device.

- **12:00** is **12:00 PM**. Noon keeps the 12 and takes PM. It is not 0 PM.

- **Colon optional**: 1430 and 14:30 parse as the same time. A single digit hour needs the colon, as in 9:05.

### How to use the Military Time Converter

1. **Type the hour from 00 to 23** — Military clocks do not use 24:00 for midnight. Use 00:00.
2. **Keep minutes from 00 to 59** — 14:60 is not 15:00 on this page. It is an invalid time.
3. **Read AM and PM from the hour, not from habit** — Anything from 12:00 up to 23:59 is PM. Anything from 00:00 up to 11:59 is AM.

### Guide

#### Where 12 goes

A 24-hour hour maps to a 12-hour hour by taking the remainder after dividing by 12, except that remainder 0 is written as 12. The suffix is PM when the original hour is 12 or more, and AM otherwise. That single rule fixes both noon and midnight. The page does not convert a duration, and it does not apply a time zone.

### FAQ

2:30 PM.

12:00 AM, midnight. 24:00 is not accepted.

**What is 12:00?**
12:00 PM, noon. It is not 12:00 AM and it is not 0:00 PM.

**Can I type 1430 without a colon?**
Yes. Four digits are read as hour and minute. 930 without a colon is ambiguous, so type 9:30.

## Leap Year Checker

URL: https://justtools.info/education-tools/leap-year-checker/
Category: Education Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-23

Check whether a year is a leap year: divisible by 4, except centuries, which must also be divisible by 400. The maths stays on your device.

### At a glance

- Leap Year Checker on Toolspire: A year is a leap year when it is divisible by **4**, unless it is divisible by **100** and not by **400**.
- **2024** is a leap year. **1900** is not. **2000** is.
- The detail says **366 days** or **365 days**, which is the consequence people need for a February calendar.
- Year **0** and negatives are rejected. The Gregorian rule is applied as the arithmetic test, not as a history of when each country adopted it.

### Features

- **The century exception is the point**: A checker that only tests “divisible by 4” marks 1900 as a leap year. This one does not.
- **2000 kept as a leap year**: Divisible by 400 puts the century back in. That case is tested, not only the 1900 rejection.
- **Day count in the detail**: 366 or 365 is the number to use when a February payslip or a day-count looks one short.

### How to use the Leap Year Checker

1. **Type the calendar year** — 2024, not “24”. A two-digit year is a different century and will be read as year 24.
2. **Test both exceptions** — Run 1900 and 2000. One is not a leap year and one is. If both say the same thing, the century rule is missing.
3. **Use 366 only when the detail says so** — Do not add 29 February to a 1900 calendar. The page’s day count is the reminder.

### Guide

#### Why centuries are special

The Julian calendar had a leap day every four years, and the year drifted. The Gregorian reform skips the leap day in century years unless the century is divisible by 400. 1900 was skipped. 2000 was not. This page applies that arithmetic. It does not try to know whether a country had switched to the Gregorian calendar by the year you type, so very old dates can disagree with a local historical calendar.

### FAQ

**Where does Leap Year Checker run?**
Leap Year Checker runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**Is 2024 a leap year?**
Yes. It is divisible by 4 and it is not a century, so it has 366 days.

**Was 1900 a leap year?**
No. It is divisible by 100 and not by 400, so the leap day was skipped. It had 365 days.

**Was 2000 a leap year?**
Yes. It is divisible by 400, so the century exception does not apply.

**Does this know when a country adopted the calendar?**
No. It is the Gregorian arithmetic test only. A date in the 1500s may have been counted differently where the reform arrived later.

## One Rep Max Calculator

URL: https://justtools.info/calculators/one-rep-max-calculator/
Category: Calculators
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-23

One Rep Max Calculator on Toolspire. Estimate a one-rep max from a weight and the reps you lifted, using the Epley formula and the Brzycki formula side by side.

### At a glance

- One Rep Max Calculator on Toolspire: **Epley:** weight × (1 + reps ÷ 30). The headline is this estimate.
- **Brzycki:** weight × 36 ÷ (37 − reps). At **1 rep** Brzycki equals the weight. Epley at 1 rep is weight × 31/30, so 100 becomes **103.3**.
- **100 for 10 reps** is an Epley max of **133.3**. The formulas disagree more as the reps rise.
- Reps above **12** are rejected. A 20-rep set is a conditioning set, not a reliable max test for these equations.

### Features

- **Two formulas, named**: You can see the disagreement instead of trusting whichever calculator hid its formula.
- **They already disagree at one rep**: Brzycki returns the weight you typed. Epley adds one thirtieth, so a single at 100 is reported as 103.3.
- **A rep cap**: Past 12 the page stops, rather than printing a max that the formulas were not checked against.

### How to use the One Rep Max Calculator

1. **Use a set that was actually hard** — A weight you stopped early on will understate the max. These formulas assume the reps were as many as you could do with decent form.
2. **Stay at 12 reps or fewer** — If the set was 15, the page will refuse. That refusal is the formula’s range, not a broken box.
3. **Compare Epley with Brzycki** — If they are far apart, do not pick the larger one as the weight to load next session.

### Guide

#### These are estimates of a single

Epley and Brzycki project a one-rep max from a set of several reps. They are curve fits, not a measurement. Even at one rep they do not match: Brzycki returns the weight, and Epley multiplies by 31/30. A true single also depends on sleep, warm-up and the lift. The page prints both numbers so a 10-rep squat is not turned into one unquestioned load. It will not tell you how to attempt that load.

### FAQ

**Where does One Rep Max Calculator run?**
One Rep Max Calculator runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**What is the Epley formula?**
Weight times (1 + reps / 30). Ten reps at 100 estimates 133.3.

**What is the Brzycki formula?**
Weight times 36 / (37 − reps). It is the second number, labelled in the detail.

**Why do the two numbers differ?**
They were fitted on different data. They already disagree at one rep: Brzycki stays on the weight, Epley multiplies by 31/30. The gap grows as reps increase. Treat the pair as a range.

**Can I use this for a 20-rep set?**
No. The page accepts 1 to 12 reps. Beyond that the estimate is too loose to print.

## Macro Calculator

URL: https://justtools.info/calculators/macro-calculator/

Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-23

Macro Calculator on Toolspire: Turn a calorie target and protein, carbohydrate and fat percentages into grams, using 4, 4 and 9 calories per gram.

### At a glance

- Macro Calculator on Toolspire: protein grams = calories × protein% ÷ 100 ÷ **4**. Carbohydrate uses the same **4**. Fat divides by **9**.
- **2,000 kcal at 30 / 40 / 30** is **150 g protein, 200 g carbohydrate, 66.7 g fat**.
- The percentages must add to **100**, within half a point. 30 / 30 / 30 is rejected rather than quietly rescaled.
- The headline is **protein grams**, because that is the number people set first. Carbs and fat are in the detail.

### Features

- **No silent rescaling**: If the three boxes do not add to 100, there is no result. A 90% split is not treated as complete.
- **4, 4 and 9**: The calorie factors are the Atwater values used on labels. Alcohol is not a fourth macro here.
- **Percent of calories, not percent of grams**: 30% protein is 30% of calories. Because fat is denser, 30% of calories is fewer grams than 30% of the food’s weight.

### How to use the Macro Calculator

1. **Start from a calorie number you already chose** — This page does not estimate how many calories you need. The calorie calculator is the place for that guess. Bring the number here.
2. **Make the three percents add to 100** — Change all three boxes. Leaving 30/40/30 and only raising protein will blank the result until the others come down.
3. **Read grams, not another percent** — The headline is grams of protein. The detail is grams of carbohydrate and fat.

### Guide

#### Percents of calories are not percents of weight

A label’s calories come mostly from protein and carbohydrate at about 4 per gram and fat at about 9. Splitting 2,000 calories 30/40/30 therefore does not mean equal-looking piles of food. Fat’s pile is lighter because each gram carries more calories. The page refuses a split that does not add to 100 so it cannot pretend the missing 10% was redistributed. It does not know your weight, your sport or what you should eat.

### FAQ

**Where does Macro Calculator run?**
Macro Calculator runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**How many grams is 30% protein of 2,000 calories?**
150 grams. 2,000 × 0.30 ÷ 4 = 150.

**Why is 30% fat not 150 grams too?**
Fat is counted at 9 calories per gram, not 4. 2,000 × 0.30 ÷ 9 is about 66.7 grams.

**What if my percents add up to 90?**
The page returns no result. Fix the split so it adds to 100. It will not spread the missing 10% for you.

**Does this tell me how much to eat?**
No. It converts a calorie target and a split you already chose into grams. It is not a meal plan.

## Body Fat Calculator

URL: https://justtools.info/calculators/body-fat-calculator/
Category: Calculators
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-23

Body Fat Calculator on Toolspire: Estimate body-fat percentage with the US Navy circumference method, typing height, neck, waist and hip in centimetres.

### At a glance

- Body Fat Calculator on Toolspire: the male equation is **495 / (1.0324 − 0.19077 × log10(waist − neck) + 0.15456 × log10(height)) − 450**, in inches.
- The female equation adds the **hip**: log10(waist + hip − neck), with the constants **1.29579, 0.35004 and 0.22100**.
- You type **centimetres**. The page divides by **2.54** before those equations, because the published constants expect inches.
- A man at **70 in, neck 15 in, waist 33 in** (177.8 cm, 38.1 cm, 83.82 cm) lands near **9.1%**.

### Features

- **Centimetres in, inches inside**: The tape most readers have is metric. The formula is not rewritten; the conversion is explicit.
- **Two equations**: The select swaps the male and female Navy formulas. Hip is used only for the female one.
- **Impossible tapes refused**: A waist that is not larger than the neck makes log of a non-positive number. The page returns nothing.

### How to use the Body Fat Calculator

1. **Measure in centimetres** — Height without shoes. Neck under the larynx. Waist at the navel for the male equation, and the hip at the widest point for the female equation.
2. **Pick the matching formula** — The constants are different. Leaving the select on male while typing a hip does not use the hip.
3. **Treat the percent as a band** — A tape pulled tight can move the result by more than a point. This is not a scan.

### Guide

#### What the Navy method actually measures

The equations estimate body fat from circumferences and height. They do not see muscle, and they punish a larger waist relative to the neck. The constants were published for inches, so a centimetre entry is converted with 2.54 and only then logged. A result outside a plausible range usually means the tape was on the wrong landmark or the wrong formula was selected. It is not a diagnosis and not a substitute for a clinical measurement.

### FAQ

**Where does Body Fat Calculator run?**
Body Fat Calculator runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**Do I type centimetres or inches?**
Centimetres. The page converts to inches because the US Navy constants were fitted in inches.

**Which waist measurement does the male formula use?**
The abdominal circumference at the navel, with the neck measured below the larynx. A chest measurement will not do.

**Why does the female formula need the hip?**
The published equation adds hip to waist and subtracts neck before the logarithm. Without a positive hip the log is refused.

**Is this the same as BMI?**
No. BMI is weight over height squared. This page never asks for weight. A muscular person can have a moderate Navy estimate and a high BMI, or the reverse.

#### A population guess, not your maximum

220 minus age is a convenient line through a cloud of real maxima. Individuals sit well above and below it. 90 to 108 beats per minute.

No. Karvonen’s formula does, and this page is not that formula. It is only 220 minus age.

It is a rough average. A supervised test can differ by more than ten beats. The page says so because the zones move with the max.

URL: https://justtools.info/calculators/ovulation-calculator/

Estimate an ovulation date as the last period plus cycle length minus 14 days, and mark a fertile window around it. Open Ovulation Calculator on Toolspire.

### At a glance

- Ovulation Calculator on Toolspire: estimated ovulation = **first day of the last period + (cycle length − 14)** days.
- A period on **1 January 2026** and a **28-day** cycle points at **15 January 2026**.
- The fertile window on the page is **5 days before** that date **through 1 day after**. For the sample, 10 January through 16 January.
- Cycles outside **20–45 days** are rejected. A one-off very short or very long cycle should not be forced through a 28-day sketch.

### Features

- **Cycle length is an input**: The page does not assume 28 unless that is what you leave in the box. A 32-day cycle moves the estimate later.
- **The 14-day luteal sketch**: The subtraction is the simplified luteal length used in calendar methods. It is not a measurement of your luteal phase.
- **A window, not a single fertile day**: Sperm survival is why the detail starts five days before the estimated ovulation, not on the day itself.

### How to use the Ovulation Calculator

1. **Use the first bleeding day** — Spotting rules differ. Use the day you would call day 1 of the cycle in a diary, and keep that definition next time.
2. **Type your usual cycle, not an average you hope for** — If the last three cycles were 26, 35 and 29, a single number is a weak estimate. The page will still run one number.
3. **Do not use the window as birth control** — A calendar cannot see a delayed ovulation. The note on the page is part of the result, not a footer to skip.

### Guide

#### What “minus 14” assumes

The sketch assumes the second half of the cycle, from ovulation to the next period, is 14 days, so ovulation sits at cycle length minus 14. Many people are close to that and many are not. Illness, travel and breastfeeding move it. The fertile window adds the days before, because sperm can wait, and one day after, as a small margin. None of this confirms that ovulation happened. A late period is a reason to take a test or talk to a clinician, not a reason to rerun the calendar.

### FAQ

**Where does Ovulation Calculator run?**
Ovulation Calculator runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**When is ovulation on a 28-day cycle?**
About 14 days after the first day of the period. A period starting 1 January 2026 estimates 15 January.

**What is the fertile window here?**
From five days before the estimated ovulation through the day after it. It is a calendar margin, not a lab result.

**What if my cycle is 35 days?**
The estimate moves to day 21 of the cycle (35 − 14), counted from the period start. Type 35. Do not leave 28.

**Can I use this to avoid pregnancy?**
No. It is not contraception. Ovulation can move, and this page cannot see that.

## Text Diff Checker

URL: https://justtools.info/text-tools/text-diff-checker/
Category: Text Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-23

Text Diff Checker on Toolspire: Compare two texts line by line with a longest-common-subsequence diff, and list the lines that were removed or added.

### At a glance

- Text Diff Checker on Toolspire: the diff is a **line LCS**. A line that appears in both texts, in an order the LCS can keep, is treated as unchanged.
- Changing dog to bird under an unchanged cat reports **1 removed and 1 added**.
- Each side is limited to **200 lines**. A longer paste is refused so the comparison stays quick in the tab.
- The detail shows up to **six removed and six added** lines, prefixed with − and +.

### Features

- **Lines, not characters**: A one-word edit marks the whole line. This is the view you want for lists, logs and paragraphs, not a code-review character diff.
- **Order is part of the match**: The LCS keeps a shared sequence. A line that moved may show as removed and added if keeping it would break the sequence.
- **A short preview**: The counts are the headline. The detail quotes the first changed lines so you do not scroll a 200-line dump.

### How to use the Text Diff Checker

1. **Paste the older text on the left** — Removed lines are lines from the left that the LCS could not keep. Added lines are new lines on the right.
2. **Keep one paragraph per line if you care about paragraphs** — A soft wrap that became a newline is a different line. Paste the texts the way you want them compared.
3. **Read a zero as a match** — “0 removed, 0 added” means every line matched in a shared order. It does not mean the files have the same name.

### Guide

#### What a line LCS will not catch

Longest common subsequence walks the two lists and keeps the longest shared sequence of equal lines. It does not understand that a sentence was edited in the middle, and it does not ignore blank lines unless you delete them first. Two hundred lines is the cap because the table is rows times columns. For a one-line typo, find-and-replace is the faster tool. For a shuffled list, expect many adds and removes.

### FAQ

**Where does Text Diff Checker run?**
Text Diff Checker runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**Does this compare words inside a line?**
No. If any character on the line differs, the whole line is removed and the new line is added.

**What does 1 removed, 1 added mean for cat/dog versus cat/bird?**
Cat was kept. Dog was removed. Bird was added.

**Why is there a 200-line cap?**
The comparison builds a grid of the two lengths. Past 200 lines a side the page refuses instead of stalling the tab.

**Will reordering identical lines show as equal?**
Not always. The algorithm needs a shared sequence. A full reversal of unique lines shows as a large change.

SERP Snippet Preview on Toolspire: Preview a page title and meta description and flag a title over 60 characters or a description outside 110–160.

### At a glance

- SERP Snippet Preview on Toolspire: A title **over 60 characters** is flagged. A title inside that length is named as inside it, with the count.

### Features

- **Character counts, not a fake ranking**: The tool tells you whether the snippet is long. It does not score keywords or promise a position.
- **Both fields at once**: Title and description are checked together because a snippet is the pair, not a title alone.

3. **Rewrite before you trust the cut** — If the title warning fires, cut words from the end. Search engines do not always cut on a word you chose.

### Guide

#### Characters are a proxy for the cut

Google sizes snippets in pixels, and the width changes. A 60-character title of wide letters can still be cut, and a 60-character title of narrow letters can fit. This page uses the character window this site already enforces — 60, and 110 to 160 — so a Toolspire page and a page you are drafting are judged the same way. It does not call a search engine and it does not store the draft.

### FAQ
