SERP Snippet Preview runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**What title length is flagged?**
Anything over 60 characters. The detail includes the count either way.

**What description length is flagged?**
Under 110 characters or over 160. Inside that band, the note says it is inside.

**Does this look up my ranking?**
No. It only measures the strings you paste. Ranking is not something a character count can know.

**Why not pixels?**
Pixel width needs the font Google is using that week. A character window is stable and matches the limit already used on this site.

## CSS Border Radius Generator

URL: https://justtools.info/css-tools/css-border-radius-generator/
Category: CSS Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-23

CSS Border Radius Generator on Toolspire: Write a border-radius declaration from four corners, and collapse it to one value when every corner matches.

### At a glance

- CSS Border Radius Generator on Toolspire: four equal corners collapse to **border-radius: 8px;** rather than repeating the value.
- Mixed corners stay in CSS order: **top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left**.
- **8, 16, 8, 0** becomes `border-radius: 8px 16px 8px 0px;`.
- Each corner must be **0–999**. Negatives are rejected. The unit on the declaration is **px**.

### Features

- **Shorthand only when it is true**: Equal corners use one length. Unequal corners never pretend to be a circle.
- **The clockwise order**: The detail names the order so a 0 on the last box is the bottom-left, not the top-left.
- **A declaration you can paste**: The headline includes the property name and the semicolon.

### How to use the CSS Border Radius Generator

1. **Set the corner you want square to 0** — A zero is valid. It is not the same as leaving a corner off the shorthand.
2. **Match all four if you want one number** — The moment one corner differs, the declaration expands to four lengths.
3. **Paste into a rule, not into a HTML attribute by accident** — The output is a CSS declaration. It is not a Tailwind class.

### Guide

#### Why equal corners collapse

CSS allows one, two or four lengths. One length is the honest form when every corner is the same, and it is what most stylesheets should keep. Four lengths are required as soon as the corners disagree, and the order is fixed by the specification: top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left. This generator does not emit elliptical radii (a slash and a second set) and it does not convert px to rem.

### FAQ

**Where does CSS Border Radius Generator run?**
CSS Border Radius Generator runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**What is the order of the four values?**
Top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left, which is clockwise from the top left.

**Why did my 8px become a single value?**
Because the other three corners are also 8. The shorthand border-radius: 8px means all four.

**Can a corner be zero?**
Yes. Zero is a square corner. The sample uses zero on the bottom left.

**Does this make a pill or a circle?**
Only if you set a radius large enough for the element’s size. The generator does not know the element’s width, so it cannot promise a pill.

## CSS Clamp Calculator

URL: https://justtools.info/css-tools/css-clamp-calculator/
Category: CSS Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-23

Build a CSS clamp() for a size that scales between two viewports, with a minimum and a maximum in pixels. The maths stays on your device.

### At a glance

- CSS Clamp Calculator on Toolspire: the slope is **(max size − min size) / (max viewport − min viewport)**. That slope times 100 is the **vw** term.
- The intercept is **min size − slope × min viewport**, so the preferred value equals the minimum at the small viewport.
- **16px to 32px from 320px to 1280px** gives `clamp(16px, 10.6667px + 1.6667vw, 32px)`.
- The maximum size must be **at least the minimum**, and the large viewport must be **wider than the small one**.

### Features

- **Viewport in pixels, slope in vw**: You describe the two screens in px. The middle term is converted to vw so the browser can interpolate.
- **Clamp keeps the ends**: The min and max arguments stop the type shrinking on a narrow phone or growing on a wide monitor.
- **Four-decimal preferred value**: The px and vw terms are rounded to four decimals, which is enough to land on the endpoints in practice.

### How to use the CSS Clamp Calculator

1. **Choose the size at the small screen and at the large screen** — 16 and 32 are a body-text example. A heading might be 28 and 48. The page does not pick a scale for you.
2. **Set the viewports where those sizes should be exact** — 320 and 1280 are the sample. Use the widths you actually design for.
3. **Paste the clamp into font-size or gap** — The declaration is the function only. Add font-size: yourself if that is the property you wanted.

### Guide

#### Where the preferred term comes from

clamp(MIN, PREFERRED, MAX) uses the preferred value when it sits between the ends. A straight line from (min viewport, min size) to (max viewport, max size) is that preferred value. Written as intercept plus slope times the viewport, and with the viewport expressed as vw, it becomes intercept-in-px plus (slope × 100) vw. At the minimum viewport the line equals the minimum size. At the maximum viewport it equals the maximum size. Outside that range, clamp holds the end you set.

### FAQ

**Where does CSS Clamp Calculator run?**
CSS Clamp Calculator runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**What does the sample clamp compute?**
16px at a 320px-wide viewport, growing to 32px at 1280px: clamp(16px, 10.6667px + 1.6667vw, 32px).

**Why is there a px term and a vw term?**
The px term is the intercept. The vw term is the slope. Together they are the straight line between your two design widths.

**Can the maximum size be smaller than the minimum?**
No. The page rejects that. A size that shrinks as the screen grows is a different design and easy to request by accident.

**Is this only for font-size?**
No. The function is a length. People use it for type, but the same string works for a fluid gap or a fluid width.

## Mailto Link Generator

URL: https://justtools.info/developer-tools/mailto-link-generator/
Category: Developer Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-23

Mailto Link Generator on Toolspire: Build a mailto link with a percent-encoded subject and body, and refuse an address that has no @ and domain.

### At a glance

- Mailto Link Generator on Toolspire: the link is `mailto:` plus the address, then `?subject=` and `&body=` when those boxes are not empty.
- Subject and body go through **URLSearchParams**, so a space becomes a plus and reserved characters are escaped.
- **hello@example.com** with subject Hello and body “Hi there” includes `subject=Hello` and `body=Hi+there`.
- An address **without @ or without a dot in the domain** is rejected. The page still cannot know the mailbox exists.

### Features

- **Encoding included**: You do not hand-escape the body. A question mark in the subject will not break the query.
- **Empty subject or body omitted**: A blank box is left off the query so the href is not full of empty parameters.
- **No send button**: The result is a link. Putting it on a page opens the visitor’s own mail app. This page does not transmit mail.

### How to use the Mailto Link Generator

1. **Type the mailbox you want the link to open** — Use the full address. A name without a domain is refused.
2. **Put the subject in its own box** — Do not prepend “Subject:” inside the body. The subject parameter is separate.
3. **Copy the href into an anchor** — The headline is the href value. Wrap it as <a href="..."> if you are writing HTML. The angle brackets are yours to add.

### Guide

#### What the visitor’s mail app receives

A mailto link does not send email by itself. The browser hands the address, subject and body to whatever program is registered for mailto. Encoding with URLSearchParams keeps an ampersand in the body from looking like a new parameter. The address check is only a shape check: one @, no spaces, and a dot after the @. It will accept a made-up domain. It will not accept two words.

### FAQ

**Where does Mailto Link Generator run?**
Mailto Link Generator runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**Does this send the email?**
No. It writes the href. The visitor’s mail program sends, if they choose to.

**How are spaces encoded?**
As plus signs, which is the form URLSearchParams uses. Mail clients accept that in a mailto query.

**What if the subject is empty?**
The subject parameter is left off. The same is true of an empty body.

**Why was my address rejected?**
It needs a local part, an @, and a domain with a dot, and no spaces. “hello@example.com” passes. “hello” does not.

3. **Copy the markup into a page** — The headline is the <table> element. Add a border in your own CSS if you want a grid.

### Guide

#### Commas inside a quoted CSV are not parsed

This generator splits on tabs when it sees one, and otherwise on every comma. It does not understand quotes. A cell written as "Smith, Ada" will break into two cells. ### FAQ

HTML Table Generator runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

The first non-empty line. It is wrapped in <thead><tr><th>.

**Can I paste from a spreadsheet?**
Yes, if the paste is tab-separated, which is what a spreadsheet copy usually is. Tabs are preferred over commas.

It becomes &lt; so the cell stays text.

No. Every cell is one column. Merged spreadsheet cells will not be reconstructed.

- **Firefox/** is its own token. Opera is recognised from **OPR/**.
- The version is the **major number** after that browser’s token, not the AppleWebKit build.

### Features

- **A deliberate order**: The bugs in naive parsers are the order. Edge is not reported as Chrome, and Chrome is not reported as Safari.
- **This device, then any string**: The box fills with this browser’s agent. Replace it to classify a string you copied from a log.

3. **Do not treat the major version as a full build** — 120 means the 120 series. The long patch number is not the headline.

### Guide

#### Why the token order matters

Chromium browsers share a user-agent shape. A string can include Mozilla, AppleWebKit, Chrome, Safari and Edg at once. The product the person is using is the most specific token: Edg for Edge, OPR for Opera, then Firefox, then Chrome, then Safari. Version is read from that token. Language and screen size are read from this browser only, and only while you have not replaced the agent string.

### FAQ

What Is My Browser runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

Edge is built on Chromium, so the string keeps Chrome/ for compatibility. The Edg/ token is what identifies Edge, and this page checks that first.

**Why is Chrome not called Safari?**
Chrome’s string includes Safari/. The page only uses Safari when Chrome/ is absent and Safari/ is present.

**What version is shown?**
The major version on the token that named the browser. Edg/120.0.0.0 is reported as Microsoft Edge 120.

**Does pasting an agent string upload it?**
No. The classification runs in this tab. Language and screen size are not attached to a string you pasted.

Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.

Indian Comma Separator on Toolspire: Group a number the Indian way: the last three digits, then pairs, so 1234567 becomes 12,34,567.

### At a glance

- Indian Comma Separator on Toolspire: digits are grouped as **3, then 2, then 2**. **1234567** becomes **12,34,567**.
- **12345678** becomes **1,23,45,678**. That is 1 crore 23 lakh 45 thousand 678.
- A number **under 1,000** is unchanged. The decimal part, if any, is not grouped.
- A leading **minus** is kept. Existing commas in the input are stripped before grouping, so you can paste 1,234,567 and get 12,34,567.

### Features

- **Not the Western comma**: 1,234,567 and 12,34,567 are the same integer with different groups. This page writes the second one.
- **Paise stay put**: 1234567.89 becomes 12,34,567.89. The dot and the fraction are not given their own commas.
- **Commas in, commas out**: Pasting a number that already has commas does not double them. They are removed, then Indian groups are applied.

### How to use the Indian Comma Separator

1. **Paste the digits without a currency sign** — ₹ and Rs are not part of the number. The box wants digits, an optional minus, and an optional decimal.
2. **Check 1234567** — The sample should read 12,34,567. If it reads 1,234,567, you are looking at a Western formatter.
3. **Keep the fraction short yourself** — The page does not round paise. 10.259 stays 10.259, with grouping only on the rupee side.

### Guide

#### Where the first comma sits

Indian place value names a thousand, then a lakh (100,000), then a crore (10,000,000). The comma follows that speech: three digits for the thousands, then pairs for lakhs and crores. Western grouping puts a comma every three digits from the right, which splits a lakh into 100,000 and hides the word people are saying. This page only regroups. It does not convert a number into the words “lakh” and “crore”; the number-to-words tool does that.

### FAQ

**Where does Indian Comma Separator run?**
Indian Comma Separator runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**How should 1234567 be written in India?**
12,34,567. That is twelve lakh, thirty-four thousand, five hundred and sixty-seven.

**What about 12345678?**
1,23,45,678. The first digit is the crore.

**Does the decimal get commas?**
No. Only the integer part is grouped. 1234567.89 becomes 12,34,567.89.

**Can I paste a number that already has commas?**
Yes. Commas are removed first, then Indian groups are applied. 1,234,567 becomes 12,34,567.

## Random Team Generator

URL: https://justtools.info/education-tools/random-team-generator/
Category: Education Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-23

Random Team Generator on Toolspire: Shuffle a list of names with Fisher–Yates and deal them into teams, so the first names typed are not stuck together.

### At a glance

- Random Team Generator on Toolspire: names are shuffled with **Fisher–Yates**, then dealt **one at a time** across the teams, like cards.
- Dealing after the shuffle stops the **top of the list** always landing in team 1 as a block.
- You need **at least as many names as teams**. Asking for 5 teams from 4 names is refused.
- The draw uses the browser’s **Math.random**. It is fine for a class. It is not a draw for prizes or money.

### Features

- **Shuffle, then deal**: A cut of the list in order would put friends who signed up together on the same team. The shuffle runs first.
- **Uneven teams stay uneven**: Seven people and three teams become groups of 3, 2 and 2. Nobody is dropped to force equal sizes.
- **A fresh deal each press**: The teams change when you press Deal. They do not change while you are still typing a name.

### How to use the Random Team Generator

1. **Put one person on each line** — Blank lines are ignored. A comma does not split a line. “Ana Lopez” stays one person.
2. **Type a team count you can fill** — Two to twenty teams, and not more teams than people.
3. **Press Deal again if the groups are only for practice** — Each press is a new shuffle. Do not keep pressing until a preferred group appears and then call it random.

### Guide

#### Why the names are dealt and not sliced

Slicing a sorted list puts the first three names on team 1. Dealing gives team 1 the first shuffled name, team 2 the next, and so on, then repeats. After a Fisher–Yates shuffle, both methods are random, but dealing keeps the team sizes as equal as the headcount allows even when you look at the order people typed. Math.random is not a cryptographic draw. Use it for groups, not for anything with a payout.

### FAQ

**Where does Random Team Generator run?**
Random Team Generator runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**How are the teams built?**
The list is shuffled, then names are dealt in order: team 1, team 2, back to team 1, until the names run out.

**Can teams be different sizes?**
Yes, when the number of people is not divisible by the number of teams. The extra people go to the earlier teams in the deal.

**What if I ask for more teams than people?**
There is no result. Every team would otherwise be empty or the page would have to invent names.

**Is this fair enough for a prize draw?**
No. It is a classroom shuffle. It is not a certified random draw, and it should not pick a winner for money.

## List Randomizer

URL: https://justtools.info/text-tools/list-randomizer/
Category: Text Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-23

Shuffle the lines of a list with Fisher–Yates, so each order of the items is equally likely. The maths stays on your device. Open List Randomizer on Toolspire.

### At a glance

- List Randomizer on Toolspire: the shuffle is **Fisher–Yates**: from the last item back to the second, swap it with an item at a random index from the start through itself.
- Every order of a given list is **equally likely**, which a “swap two random items once” shuffle is not.
- Blank lines are dropped. **Fewer than two items** is refused, because there is nothing to reorder.
- The button draws with **Math.random**. The same list can come back in the original order; that outcome is allowed.

### Features

- **Lines stay whole**: A line is one item, even if it contains commas or spaces. The shuffle does not split phrases.
- **A new order on each press**: Typing does not reshuffle under your cursor. Only the button does.
- **The original is still in the box**: The textarea is not replaced. The shuffled copy is the result, so you can shuffle again from the same source.

### How to use the List Randomizer

1. **Put one item on each line** — A paragraph in a single line is one item. Break the list first if each word should move on its own.
2. **Press shuffle** — The result is a new order of the same lines. Duplicates you typed stay duplicated.
3. **Shuffle again from the box, not from the result** — The source stays put. If you paste the result back into the box, you are shuffling that new order, which is also fair.

### Guide

#### What “equally likely” requires

Fisher–Yates walks the list once and swaps each index i with a uniformly chosen index from 0 through i. Done from the end, that produces each permutation with the same probability. Swapping two random positions a fixed number of times does not. This page uses the single-pass method. Math.random is suitable for a playlist, a revision order or a reading list. It is not a draw for money.

### FAQ

**Where does List Randomizer run?**
List Randomizer runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**Does each order have the same chance?**
Yes, for the Fisher–Yates shuffle this page uses. That includes the original order, which will sometimes come back.

**Will duplicate lines be merged?**
No. Two identical lines are two items and both survive.

**Can I shuffle a single line?**
No. One item has only one order. Add a second line.

**Does the box change?**
No. The source stays in the textarea. The shuffled lines are the result under it.

Ohms Law Calculator on Toolspire: Solve volts, amps or ohms from V = I × R by leaving one box blank, and show the power in watts for that pair.

- Ohms Law Calculator on Toolspire: **V = I × R**. 2 amps and 5 ohms give **10 volts**.
- **I = V ÷ R** and **R = V ÷ I**. 10 volts across 5 ohms is **2 amps**. 10 volts at 2 amps is **5 ohms**.
- Power in the detail is **P = V × I**, in watts. For 10 V and 2 A that is **20 W**.
- Leave **exactly one** box empty. Zero resistance cannot give a current, and zero current cannot give a resistance.

- **One unknown**: The empty box is solved. Three filled boxes are not checked against each other, because you did not say which number is wrong.
- **Watts beside the answer**: Once two of V, I and R are known, power is fixed too, and it is written in the detail.
- **DC and ideal**: There is no AC impedance, no temperature rise, and no wire size. Those are not this equation.

### How to use the Ohms Law Calculator

1. **Clear the quantity the problem asks for** — If the question asks for voltage, leave voltage empty and type current and resistance.
2. **Use volts, amps and ohms** — Milliamps must be converted. 200 mA is 0.2 A. The page will not divide by 1000 for you.
3. **Read watts only as V times I** — The detail is that product. It is not a rating for a cable or a fuse.

### Guide

#### The equation and nothing past it

Ohm’s law here is the DC relationship between voltage, current and resistance for an ideal resistor. Power is the product of voltage and current once those are known. The page stops there. It does not choose a wire, a fuse or a supply, and it must not be used as a reason to open a wall, a panel or a live circuit. Alternating current, reactance and a hot filament all leave this model.

### FAQ

**What current is 10 volts across 5 ohms?**
2 amps. Leave the current box empty.

**Why is a zero resistance rejected when solving for current?**
Current would be voltage divided by zero. The page returns no result instead of infinity.

**Can I use this for house wiring?**

## Download Time Calculator

URL: https://justtools.info/network-tools/download-time-calculator/
Category: Internet & Network Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-23

Download Time Calculator on Toolspire: Work out how long a file takes at a megabit link speed, using decimal bytes and one million bits per second.

### At a glance

- Download Time Calculator on Toolspire: time is **size in bytes × 8 ÷ bits per second**. A byte is eight bits, which is the factor people forget.
- **1 GB at 100 Mbps is 1 min 20 sec.** 1 GB here is 1,000,000,000 bytes, and 100 Mbps is 100,000,000 bits a second.
- **1 Mbps is 0.125 MB/s** of decimal bytes. The detail prints that MB/s figure next to the clock time.
- The page does **not measure** the connection. Packet headers, Wi-Fi and a busy server all make a real transfer slower than this division.

### Features

- **Megabits in, minutes out**: The speed box is Mbps, the unit an ISP prints. The size box is MB, GB or TB of decimal bytes.
- **The 8× is visible**: The detail shows MB/s as Mbps divided by 8, so a 100 Mbps line is not treated as 100 megabytes a second.
- **A clock, not a raw second count**: Eighty seconds is shown as 1 min 20 sec. The unrounded seconds stay in the detail.

### How to use the Download Time Calculator

1. **Type the file size in decimal units** — A shop that says 1 GB almost always means 1,000,000,000 bytes. Use GB for that. A 1024-based gibibyte is about 7% larger and is not what this page divides.
2. **Type the link speed in Mbps** — Use the rate you expect to get, not the number on the router box, if you already know the line is slower than the plan.
3. **Read the clock as a floor** — The result is the time if every bit of the plan is payload. Add time for a weak signal or a capped server.

### Guide

#### Why 100 Mbps is not 100 MB/s

Network speeds are sold in megabits. Files are sized in megabytes. There are eight bits in a byte, so a 100 Mbps plan moves 12.5 decimal megabytes a second when every bit is file data. Dividing a gigabyte by 100, as if the units matched, gives 10 seconds and is wrong by a factor of eight. This page keeps the units apart: you pick MB, GB or TB, you type Mbps, and the 8× happens in the formula. It does not open a socket and it does not time your own line. The speed test is the page that does that.

### FAQ

**Where does Download Time Calculator run?**
Download Time Calculator runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**How long is a 1 GB download at 100 Mbps?**
1 minute 20 seconds, using a decimal gigabyte and a decimal megabit. 1,000,000,000 bytes × 8 ÷ 100,000,000 bits per second = 80 seconds.

**Is a GB here 1024 megabytes?**
No. MB, GB and TB on this page are powers of 1,000. A gibibyte (1024³) would take about 7% longer at the same megabit rate.

**Why is my real download slower?**
The formula assumes the link is full of file bytes. TCP headers, Wi-Fi retries, a busy disk and a server that will not send that fast all add time.

**Does this test my connection?**
No. You type the speed. The internet speed test is the tool that measures download, upload, ping and jitter.

Data Usage Calculator on Toolspire: Turn a steady megabit rate and the hours you use it into gigabytes. One megabit is one million bits a second.

- Idle time is **not counted**. If the link is full for one hour and quiet for the rest, type 1, not 24.

### Features

- **A full pipe, for the hours you name**: The speed is assumed constant. It is not an average of a speed test taken once.
- **Decimal gigabytes**: The headline matches the gigabytes an ISP quota usually means: powers of 1,000, not 1,024.

### Guide

An ISP quota is a pile of bytes. A plan speed is a rate. They meet only when you say how long the rate is sustained. This page does that multiplication and converts bits to decimal gigabytes. If you know the file size instead of the duration, the download-time calculator answers the other direction.

### FAQ

**Where does Data Usage Calculator run?**
Data Usage Calculator runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**How many GB is 10 Mbps for one hour?**
4.5 decimal gigabytes. Ten million bits a second for 3,600 seconds is 36 billion bits, which is 4.5 billion bytes.

**Why not 24 hours by default?**
Because almost nobody fills the pipe all day. The sample is one hour. Change the hours to match the transfer, not the time the computer is switched on.

**Is this the same as the download-time page?**
No. That page starts from a file size and a speed and returns a clock time. This page starts from a speed and a duration and returns gigabytes.

**Does a speed test replace the Mbps box?**
Only as a hint. A ten-second test is not the rate of an evening. Type the rate you believe holds for the hours in the second box.

## Uptime Calculator

URL: https://justtools.info/network-tools/uptime-calculator/
Category: Internet & Network Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-23

Uptime Calculator on Toolspire: Turn an availability percent such as 99.9 into downtime for a day, a 30-day month and a 365-day year. It is arithmetic.

### At a glance

- Uptime Calculator on Toolspire: downtime fraction = **(100 − percent) ÷ 100**. At 99.9% that fraction is 0.001.
- A **365-day year** at 99.9% allows **8 h 45 min 36 sec**. The year is 365 × 86,400 seconds, not 365.25.
- The same 99.9% allows about **1 min 26 sec a day** and **43 min 12 sec in a 30-day month**.
- **100% is 0 seconds.** A percent above 100 or below 0 is rejected. This page does not watch a host.

### Features

- **Three windows from one percent**: The headline is the year. The detail is the day and a 30-day month, so a monthly SLA and a yearly SLA are not mixed up.
- **A 365-day year on purpose**: Leap seconds and the extra day in a leap year are left out so 99.9% has one published answer.
- **Nearest second**: 86.4 seconds in a day at 99.9% is shown as 1 min 26 sec. The raw product is not left as a long decimal.

### How to use the Uptime Calculator

1. **Type the percent from the agreement** — 99.9 and 99.99 are different promises. Do not round the contract’s figure before you type it.
2. **Read the year on the headline** — That is the usual way an annual SLA is spoken. The month in the detail is 30 days, not “this calendar month”.
3. **Do not treat the number as a ping result** — Nothing is contacted. If you need to see whether a path is up right now, this page will not tell you.

### Guide

#### What the nines actually buy

Each extra nine cuts the allowed downtime by ten. Two nines, 99%, still leave about 3.65 days in a 365-day year. Three nines, 99.9%, leave 8 hours 45 minutes 36 seconds. Four nines leave about 52 minutes 34 seconds. The page is that multiplication and nothing else: no probe, no incident clock, no exclusion for planned maintenance. If the contract excludes a maintenance window, subtract that window yourself. The calculator will not.

### FAQ

**Where does Uptime Calculator run?**
Uptime Calculator runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**How much downtime is 99.9% in a year?**
8 hours, 45 minutes and 36 seconds, in a year of 365 days. Per day it is 1 minute 26 seconds, after rounding 86.4 seconds to the nearest second.

**Why 365 days and not 365.25?**
So the answer does not change with a leap-year average. A contract that defines a year differently needs that year length, not this one.

**Does 100% mean the service cannot fail?**
It means the arithmetic allows zero seconds. It does not mean a real service has been, or will be, perfect.

**Will this ping my server?**
No. You type a percent. The page never opens a connection.

Port Number Lookup on Toolspire. Look up a well-known TCP or UDP port, or a service name such as SSH, HTTPS or MySQL, from a fixed list. No host is scanned.

### At a glance

- Port Number Lookup on Toolspire: **443 TCP is HTTPS.** That is the port a browser uses for a site with TLS.
- **22 TCP is SSH**, including SFTP and Git over SSH. **53 is DNS**, usually UDP, and TCP when the answer is large.
- Mail is split on purpose: **25** is server-to-server SMTP, **587** is submission from a mail app, **465** is SMTPS.
- The list is fixed. **Nothing is contacted**, and port 1 returning no row does not mean a host has that port closed.

### Features

- **Number or name**: 443 returns one row. Typing mysql returns 3306. A partial name can return several rows, listed in the detail.
- **Protocol on the row**: DHCP is labelled UDP. HTTPS is labelled TCP. DNS is labelled TCP/UDP because both are real.
- **A short note, not a scan**: Each row says what the port is for. The page never sends a packet to an address you did not type, and there is no address box.

### How to use the Port Number Lookup

1. **Type the number or the service** — Use 443, or https, or ssh. The match is the list on this page, not a live host.
2. **Read the protocol** — A firewall rule that says TCP 53 does not cover ordinary DNS queries, which are UDP. The row says which one the service usually uses.
3. **Treat a miss as “not in the list”** — Thousands of registered ports are absent. Absence is not a closed port and not an unused port.

### Guide

#### A pocket list, not a port scan

People search a port because a log, a firewall rule or an error named a number. The useful answer is the service name and whether it is TCP, UDP or both. This page answers from a short list of those well-known services: the web, mail, DNS, SSH, databases and a few admin ports. Redis on 6379 and MongoDB on 27017 are included with the note that they should not face the public internet.

### FAQ

**Where does Port Number Lookup run?**
Port Number Lookup runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**What is port 443?**
HTTPS on TCP. It is HTTP inside TLS, the port a browser uses for a secure site.

**What is port 22?**
SSH on TCP. File transfer with SFTP and Git over SSH use it too.

**Why are there three SMTP ports?**
Port 25 is how mail servers hand mail to each other. Port 587 is how a person’s mail app submits a message. Port 465 is SMTP wrapped in TLS from the start. They are not interchangeable.

**Does a missing port mean it is closed?**
No. The page did not look at a computer. The number is simply not one of the named rows.

## MAC Address Generator

URL: https://justtools.info/network-tools/mac-address-generator/
Category: Internet & Network Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-23

MAC Address Generator on Toolspire. Check a MAC address, name the unicast and local-admin bits. No account is required.

### At a glance

- MAC Address Generator on Toolspire: A MAC is **48 bits**, shown as six hex bytes. Colons, dashes and Cisco groups of four (`001A.2B3C.4D5E`) all parse.
- The **lowest bit of the first byte** is the group bit. 1 means multicast or broadcast. 0 means unicast.
- The **next bit** is the local bit. 1 means locally administered. 0 means a universally administered, vendor-style address.
- Generate sets those bits to **local and unicast** (`xxxxxx10` in the low two bits). It does not copy a real vendor prefix, and it does not look one up.

### Features

- **Read the two bits that matter**: The detail says unicast or multicast, and local or universal. The other bytes are not turned into a manufacturer name.
- **One canonical spelling**: Whatever separators you paste, the headline is lowercase hex with colons.
- **A lab address, not a disguise**: The button builds a local unicast address for a virtual machine or a lab you are allowed to configure. It is not a way onto someone else’s network.

### How to use the MAC Address Generator

1. **Paste an address to read it** — Colons, dashes or Cisco dots are fine. You need 12 hex digits. Anything else is refused.
2. **Read local versus universal** — A burned-in adapter address has the local bit clear. An address a hypervisor invented usually has it set.
3. **Generate only for a machine you may configure** — Press the button, then use the result in a lab or a VM setting you control. Do not put it on a network where you are not allowed to choose the address.

### Guide

#### Why the generated address is locally administered

The IEEE leaves a bit so that software can mint an address without colliding with a factory prefix. That is the local bit, the second-lowest bit of the first octet. This generator sets it and clears the group bit, so the result is a unicast address that does not pretend to be a particular vendor’s hardware. There is no manufacturer database on the page, because a partial list would mis-name most addresses. Use the result where you are allowed to set a virtual adapter. It is not a tool for slipping past an access list on a network you do not administer.

### FAQ

**Where does MAC Address Generator run?**
MAC Address Generator runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**What does locally administered mean?**
The address was chosen by software or by an administrator, not burned into a card by a manufacturer. The second-lowest bit of the first octet is 1.

**What is the multicast bit?**
The lowest bit of the first octet. When it is 1, the address names a group, not a single adapter. ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff is the broadcast address and that bit is set.

**Will this tell me the vendor?**
No. The other five bytes are not looked up. A vendor guess from a short table would be wrong too often to print.

**Can I use a generated address on any network?**
Only on a lab or a virtual machine you are allowed to configure. The page will not help you substitute an address to get past someone else’s filter.

## CIDR Overlap Checker

URL: https://justtools.info/network-tools/cidr-overlap-checker/
Category: Internet & Network Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-23

CIDR Overlap Checker on Toolspire. Compare two IPv4 CIDR prefixes and report whether one contains the other, they are the same range, or they are disjoint.

### At a glance

- CIDR Overlap Checker on Toolspire: each prefix is masked to its **network address and broadcast address**, then the two ranges are compared.
- **10.0.0.0/8 contains 10.1.2.0/24.** Reverse the boxes and the result is “second contains first”.
- **10.0.0.0/24 and 10.0.1.0/24 are disjoint.** Same-size neighbours do not share an address.
- A halfway overlap is **not a possible answer** for two valid CIDR blocks. They nest, they match, or they sit apart. IPv6 is not compared here.

### Features

- **Four plain answers**: Same range, first contains second, second contains first, or disjoint. The detail shows both broadcast ranges.
- **The host bits are masked off**: 10.1.2.9/24 is the same block as 10.1.2.0/24. The typed host does not create a different range.
- **IPv4 only**: The subnet calculator is the page for IPv6, VLSM and a single block’s host count. This page only compares two IPv4 prefixes.

### How to use the CIDR Overlap Checker

1. **Type two prefixes with a slash** — 10.0.0.0/8 and 10.1.2.0/24 are the sample. A mask written as 255.255.255.0 is not accepted here.
2. **Read contains before you read overlap** — If the result says contains, every address of the smaller block is inside the larger one. There is no partial case to worry about.
3. **Use the subnet page for the host list** — This page does not count usable hosts or split a block. It only answers how the two ranges sit.

### Guide

#### Why CIDR blocks do not overlap halfway

A CIDR prefix is a power-of-two range that starts on its own alignment. Take two of them. Either one range sits entirely inside the other, they are the same range, or they share no address. The awkward case people fear — the first half of one block colliding with the second half of another — cannot happen when both inputs are real prefixes. If a diagram shows that kind of overlap, one of the boxes is not a CIDR block. This checker masks each input, compares the two closed ranges, and uses those four words. It does not plan VLSM and it does not speak IPv6.

### FAQ

**Where does CIDR Overlap Checker run?**
CIDR Overlap Checker runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**Does 10.0.0.0/8 contain 10.1.2.0/24?**
Yes. The result is “First contains second”. Swap the boxes and it becomes “Second contains first”.

**Can two different /24 networks overlap?**
No. Two different blocks of the same size are disjoint. 10.0.0.0/24 and 10.0.1.0/24 do not share an address.

**What if I type 10.1.2.9/24?**
The host bits are cleared. That is the block 10.1.2.0–10.1.2.255, the same as 10.1.2.0/24.

**Where do I calculate hosts or IPv6?**
On the IP subnet calculator. This page only compares two IPv4 prefixes.

### How to use the IPv4 Address Converter

1. **Paste one spelling** — Use 192.168.0.1, or 3232235521, or 0xc0a80001. Do not include a prefix length.
2. **Check the integer against the hex** — The hex is the same 32-bit number. 0xc0 is 192, 0xa8 is 168, 0x00 is 0, 0x01 is 1.
3. **Leave subnet questions on the other page** — If you need the network or the broadcast, open the subnet calculator. This page will not guess a mask.

### Guide

#### One 32-bit number, four ways of writing it

An IPv4 address is an unsigned 32-bit integer that people print as four decimal bytes. Hex is the same integer with a 0x prefix, eight digits so leading zeros stay visible. Binary is those four bytes in bits, because that is how a mask lines up in a textbook. 192.168.0.1 is the running example: 3,232,235,521, 0xc0a80001, and 11000000.10101000.00000000.00000001. The converter stops there. It does not decide whether the address is private, and it does not find a subnet.

### FAQ

**Where does IPv4 Address Converter run?**
IPv4 Address Converter runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**What is 192.168.0.1 as an integer?**
3,232,235,521. In hex that is 0xc0a80001.

**What is 192 in binary?**
11000000. The full address 192.168.0.1 is 11000000.10101000.00000000.00000001.

**Can I paste a hex address?**
Yes, with a 0x prefix and at most eight hex digits, such as 0xc0a80001.

**Does this apply a subnet mask?**
No. There is no prefix box. Network and broadcast addresses are on the subnet calculator.

## Punycode Converter

URL: https://justtools.info/network-tools/punycode-converter/
Category: Internet & Network Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-23

Punycode Converter on Toolspire. Convert an international domain name to ASCII punycode and back, using the xn-- prefix from RFC 3492.

### At a glance

- Punycode Converter on Toolspire: punycode is **RFC 3492**. A label that needs it is prefixed with **xn--**.
- **münchen.de** encodes to **xn--mnchen-3ya.de**. The ASCII label “de” is not encoded.
- **bücher** encodes to **xn--bcher-kva**. Pasting that ASCII form decodes back to bücher.
- A scheme, a slash, a space or an **@** is rejected. This page converts a domain, not a full URL.

### Features

- **Encode and decode in one box**: Unicode labels become xn-- in the headline. xn-- labels become Unicode in the detail. ASCII labels pass through.
- **One label at a time**: www.münchen.de encodes only the middle label. The dots stay dots.
- **The algorithm is on the page**: The result does not ask a DNS server. A name can be converted even when it is not registered.

### How to use the Punycode Converter

1. **Paste the domain without https://** — münchen.de is enough. A path or a query string is refused so it is not mistaken for part of a label.
2. **Read ASCII on the headline** — That is the form older DNS software stores. The detail is the Unicode spelling.
3. **Look the name up elsewhere if you need records** — Conversion is not registration and not a DNS answer. The DNS lookup tool is the one that asks resolvers.

### Guide

#### Why only some labels grow an xn--

A domain is a sequence of labels separated by dots. Punycode is defined for one label. Letters that already fit in ASCII stay as they are, which is why “de” and “www” do not gain a prefix. A label with a character outside ASCII is encoded and written as xn-- plus the punycode. münchen.de therefore becomes xn--mnchen-3ya.de, and bücher becomes xn--bcher-kva. The page implements RFC 3492 for that conversion. It does not speak to a DNS server, and it will not accept a URL with a scheme, because the slashes are not part of the name.

### FAQ

**Where does Punycode Converter run?**
Punycode Converter runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**What is the punycode for münchen.de?**
xn--mnchen-3ya.de. The label de is already ASCII, so only münchen is encoded.

**What is bücher in punycode?**
xn--bcher-kva. Pasting that value back prints bücher in the Unicode line.

**Does this check that the domain exists?**
No. Any string of labels can be converted. Existence is a DNS question, and the DNS lookup tool is the one that asks.

**Can I paste a full URL?**
No. Drop the scheme and the path first. A slash, a space or an @ is rejected so it cannot hide inside a label.

## Present Value Calculator

URL: https://justtools.info/calculators/present-value-calculator/
Category: Calculators
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-23

Discount a future lump sum back to today with present value = future ÷ (1 + rate) raised to the number of years. Open Present Value Calculator on Toolspire.

### At a glance

- Present Value Calculator on Toolspire: present value = **future ÷ (1 + rate)^years**, compounded once a year.
- **₹121 in 2 years at 10%** is **₹100** today. 121 ÷ 1.21 = 100.
- A higher rate or a longer wait **shrinks** today’s value. The future cheque does not change.
- This is one lump sum. A stream of payments is the NPV page, not this one.

### Features

- **One future cheque**: Type the amount you will receive once, the yearly rate, and how many years away it is.
- **Annual compounding**: The divisor is (1 + annual rate) to the power of whole or fractional years. It is not divided by 12.
- **The worked example is 121 and 10%**: Two years turns 1.10 × 1.10 = 1.21, and 121 ÷ 1.21 lands on 100.

### How to use the Present Value Calculator

1. **Type the amount you will actually get** — Use the future rupee figure, not today’s price of the thing you hope to buy.
2. **Use a discount rate you could earn elsewhere** — If a fixed deposit pays 7%, try 7% rather than a hopeful 12%.
3. **Read a smaller number as the cost of waiting** — The gap between the future amount and the headline is what those years of delay are worth at that rate.

### Guide

#### Why divide instead of multiply

Compound interest asks what a rupee becomes later. Present value asks what a later rupee is worth now, so the same factor is used as a divisor. ₹121 ÷ (1.10)² is ₹100. The page does not subtract inflation on top of the rate you type. If you want purchasing power, put a real rate in the box yourself.

### FAQ

**Where does Present Value Calculator run?**
Present Value Calculator runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**What is the present value of ₹121 in two years at 10%?**
₹100. The growth factor is 1.21, and 121 divided by 1.21 is 100.

**Is the rate monthly?**
No. 10 means 10% a year, applied once a year. A monthly rate belongs in a different model.

**What if the rate is zero?**
The present value equals the future amount. Waiting earns nothing, so a rupee later is still a rupee now.

**How is this different from the lumpsum calculator?**
Lumpsum multiplies today’s money forward. This page divides a future sum backward.

## Effective Annual Rate Calculator

URL: https://justtools.info/calculators/effective-annual-rate-calculator/
Category: Calculators
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-23

Effective Annual Rate Calculator on Toolspire: Turn a nominal annual rate and a compounding count into the effective annual rate, (1 + r/n)^n − 1.

### At a glance

- Effective Annual Rate Calculator on Toolspire: EAR = **(1 + nominal/periods)^periods − 1**.
- **12% compounded monthly** is **(1.01)^12 − 1**, about **12.68%**.
- Compounding **once a year** makes EAR equal the nominal rate.
- More compounds **raise** the effective rate. The nominal percent in the advert does not move.

### Features

- **Periods are a count, not a percent**: 12 means monthly. 4 means quarterly. 1 means the effective rate equals the nominal rate.
- **The formula is the definition**: Nothing is annualised by multiplying a monthly rate by 12. That product is the nominal rate you already typed.
- **12.68 is the check**: Twelve percent with twelve compounds should read 12.68% after rounding to two decimals.

### How to use the Effective Annual Rate Calculator

1. **Copy the advertised yearly rate** — If the note says 12% per annum compounded monthly, type 12 and 12. Do not type 1.
2. **Count the compounds** — Monthly is 12, quarterly is 4, half-yearly is 2, daily is 365 if they truly compound every day.
3. **Compare EAR with a once-a-year deposit** — A 12% annual deposit and a 12% monthly deposit are not the same deal. The gap is this page’s result minus 12.

### Guide

#### Nominal is the label, effective is the year

Banks often quote a nominal yearly rate and then compound more than once. Each compound adds interest on interest inside the year, so a rupee grows by more than the printed percent. (1 + 0.12/12)^12 − 1 is the extra. This page does not know fees, tax or a premature-withdrawal penalty.

### FAQ

**Where does Effective Annual Rate Calculator run?**
Effective Annual Rate Calculator runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**What is 12% compounded monthly as an effective rate?**
About 12.68% a year. Each month multiplies the balance by 1.01, twelve times.

**What if it compounds once a year?**
The effective rate equals the nominal rate. Type 1 in the periods box.

**Is EAR the same as APR?**
No. APR is often a nominal or a fee-inclusive borrowing label. EAR here is only the compound-growth identity from the rate and the count you type.

**Why not just multiply 1% by 12?**
That product is 12%, the nominal rate. Effective rate compounds the 1% on the growing balance.

## Sinking Fund Calculator

URL: https://justtools.info/calculators/sinking-fund-calculator/
Category: Calculators
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-23

Find the equal year-end deposit that grows to a target, using payment = target × r ÷ ((1 + r)^years − 1). The maths stays on your device.

### At a glance

- Sinking Fund Calculator on Toolspire: with interest, the deposit is **target × r ÷ ((1 + r)^years − 1)**, paid at each year end.
- At **0%**, the deposit is **target ÷ years**. ₹1,000 over 5 years is **₹200**.
- The deposits are **yearly**, not monthly. A monthly SIP is a different formula.
- A higher rate **cuts** the deposit, because interest does more of the work.

### Features

- **Year-end deposits**: The formula assumes each deposit arrives at the end of the year and then has the remaining years to earn.
- **A zero-rate identity**: No interest means an even split. That is the check that the page is not sneaking in a return.
- **One target, one rate**: The target does not step up, and the rate does not change halfway through.

### How to use the Sinking Fund Calculator

1. **Type the amount you need on the final day** — Include the whole target. Do not subtract what you have already saved unless you reduce the target yourself.
2. **Keep the rate annual** — 8 means 8% a year. Do not type a monthly rate.
3. **Compare with a zero rate** — Run 0% once. The deposit should be the target divided by the years. Anything else is a bug, not a feature.

### Guide

#### A sinking fund is the reverse of compound growth

Compound interest starts from a deposit and walks forward. A sinking fund starts from the pile you need and walks backward to the equal year-end payment that reaches it. At a zero rate that payment is the target divided by the years. With interest, each earlier deposit has fewer years of growth than a lump sum placed today, which is why the payment is larger than target ÷ (1+r)^years. Tax and a missed year are not in the figure.

### FAQ

**Where does Sinking Fund Calculator run?**
Sinking Fund Calculator runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**What yearly deposit builds ₹1,000 in 5 years at 0%?**
₹200. With no interest the target is simply split into five equal deposits.

**Why is this not the SIP calculator?**
A SIP here would be monthly. This page deposits once each year, at the end of the year.

**Does a higher rate mean I save less?**
Yes. The target stays put, so more growth means a smaller deposit from you.

**When is the deposit made?**
At the end of each year. A deposit on 1 January would earn a full extra year and needs a different formula.

## Straight-Line Depreciation

URL: https://justtools.info/calculators/straight-line-depreciation/
Category: Calculators
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-23

Straight-Line Depreciation on Toolspire: Spread an asset’s cost minus salvage in equal yearly depreciation: (cost − salvage) ÷ useful life.

### At a glance

- Straight-Line Depreciation on Toolspire: annual charge = **(cost − salvage) ÷ years**.
- **₹1,000 cost, ₹100 salvage, 5 years** is **₹180** a year.
- After the life, the book value equals the **salvage**, because the charges add up to cost minus salvage.
- Salvage **above cost** is rejected. Depreciation would otherwise add value.

### Features

- **The same charge every year**: Year 5 is the same rupee amount as year 1. That is the point of straight line.
- **Salvage is not depreciated**: Only the gap between cost and what you expect to recover is spread.
- **Life is whole years**: The page rounds the life to a year count before it divides.

### How to use the Straight-Line Depreciation

1. **Use the capitalised cost** — Include what you capitalised. Do not also deduct the same installation cost as an expense.
2. **Type a salvage you can defend** — Zero is allowed. A salvage higher than cost is not.
3. **Do not use this for a block of assets under tax law** — Income-tax written-down value is a different method. The declining-balance page is closer to that shape, and even that is not a return.

### Guide

#### Equal charges, then salvage remains

Straight line takes the portion of cost you do not expect to recover and divides it by the useful life. Five charges of ₹180 on a ₹1,000 asset with ₹100 salvage use up ₹900 and leave ₹100. The method ignores that a machine often loses more value in year one. It also ignores tax blocks, extra shift depreciation and a change of estimate.

### FAQ

**Where does Straight-Line Depreciation run?**
Straight-Line Depreciation runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**What is the yearly charge on ₹1,000 with ₹100 salvage over 5 years?**
₹180. The depreciable amount is ₹900, and 900 ÷ 5 is 180.

**Does the charge fall each year?**
No. Falling charges are the declining-balance method. Straight line repeats the same amount.

**Can salvage be zero?**
Yes. The whole cost is then spread across the life.

**Is this the income-tax depreciation rate?**
No. Tax depreciation in India is generally a block written-down-value calculation. This page is the equal-charge method only.

## Declining Balance Depreciation

URL: https://justtools.info/calculators/declining-balance-depreciation/
Category: Calculators
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-23

Apply a fixed percent to the opening book value, and show year-one depreciation plus the book value left. The maths stays on your device.

### At a glance

- Declining Balance Depreciation on Toolspire: year-one depreciation = **opening book × rate**.
- **₹1,000 at 20%** is **₹200**, and the closing book is **₹800**.
- Next year the same percent applies to **₹800**, not to the original ₹1,000.
- The rate is the percent you type. The page does not look up a tax block rate.

### Features

- **Only the next year**: The headline is this year’s charge. The detail is the book value the following year would start from.
- **Percent of what remains**: The base is the opening book, which already excludes earlier years’ depreciation if you type that reduced figure.
- **No salvage floor**: The method can keep charging forever on paper. A salvage stop is a policy you apply outside this one-year sum.

### How to use the Declining Balance Depreciation

1. **Type this year’s opening book, not the original invoice if years have passed** — After one 20% year, a ₹1,000 asset opens the next year at ₹800. Type 800 for year two.
2. **Type the percent, not a fraction** — 20 means 20%. 0.2 would be read as a fifth of one percent.
3. **Use straight line if the charge must be equal** — This page will not flatten the charge. Equal amounts are the other depreciation page.

### Guide

#### The percent is fixed and the base falls

Declining balance multiplies whatever book value you still have by the same percent. Twenty percent of ₹1,000 is ₹200, so the next opening book is ₹800, and twenty percent of that would be ₹160. The page stops after one year so you can see that hand-off. It does not build a tax block, add new purchases, or stop at a salvage value.

### FAQ

**Where does Declining Balance Depreciation run?**
Declining Balance Depreciation runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**What is 20% declining balance on ₹1,000?**
₹200 of depreciation, and ₹800 of book value left.

**Why is year two not ₹200 as well?**
Because the base fell to ₹800. Twenty percent of 800 is 160. Type 800 to see that year.

**Is this the Income Tax Act rate?**
Only if the percent you type is the rate for that block. The page does not store those rates.

**How do I force an equal charge?**
Use the straight-line page. Declining balance is unequal by design.

## Current Ratio Calculator

URL: https://justtools.info/calculators/current-ratio-calculator/
Category: Calculators
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-23

Current Ratio Calculator on Toolspire. Divide current assets by current liabilities. A result of 2 means there are two rupees of short-term assets per rupee.

### At a glance

- Current Ratio Calculator on Toolspire: current ratio = **current assets ÷ current liabilities**.
- **200 ÷ 100 = 2**. Two rupees of short-term assets stand behind each rupee of short-term bills.
- Inventory, receivables and cash all sit in the asset box. Nothing is removed.
- Liabilities of **zero** are rejected. The ratio would be undefined.

### Features

- **Both sides are current**: Do not type plant or a long-term loan. Those belong on a different statement line.
- **Inventory is included**: That is the difference from the quick ratio, which subtracts stock.
- **A plain division**: There is no “good” threshold built in. 2 is the sample, not a pass mark.

### How to use the Current Ratio Calculator

1. **Use the same date for both numbers** — A March asset total against a June liability total is not a ratio, it is two photographs.
2. **Keep stock in the assets** — If you want stock out, use the quick-ratio page instead of subtracting here and forgetting.
3. **Read 1 as a one-for-one cover** — Below 1, current bills exceed current assets on the numbers you typed.

### Guide

#### A liquidity snapshot, not a credit rating

The current ratio lines up everything due within a year on the asset side against everything due within a year on the liability side. It treats slow stock the same as cash. That is why a high ratio can still hide a warehouse nobody wants to buy. The page only divides the two totals you type.

### FAQ

**Where does Current Ratio Calculator run?**
Current Ratio Calculator runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**What is 200 over 100?**
A current ratio of 2.

**Should inventory be included?**
Yes on this page. Exclude it on the quick-ratio page if you want a tighter test.

**What does below 1 mean?**
Current liabilities are larger than current assets, on the figures you typed. It is not by itself a default.

**Why is zero liabilities rejected?**
Division by zero is not a ratio. A firm with no current bills has no current-ratio number.

URL: https://justtools.info/calculators/quick-ratio-calculator/

Quick Ratio Calculator on Toolspire. Subtract inventory from current assets, then divide by current liabilities. This is the acid-test ratio.

### At a glance

- Quick Ratio Calculator on Toolspire: quick ratio = **(current assets − inventory) ÷ current liabilities**.
- **200 − 50 = 150**, and **150 ÷ 100 = 1.5**.
- Inventory larger than current assets is rejected, because the quick assets would be negative from a typing error.
- The current ratio on the same numbers is **2**, because it keeps the ₹50 of stock.

### Features

- **Stock comes out**: The subtraction is the whole point. Cash, receivables and other current assets stay.
- **The current ratio is named beside it**: The detail reminds you what the looser ratio would have been.
- **No prepaid-expense debate**: Anything you leave inside current assets, other than the inventory you type, stays in the quick total.

### How to use the Quick Ratio Calculator

1. **Make sure inventory is part of the asset total** — If stock is already excluded from the asset box, type 0 for inventory or you will subtract it twice.
2. **Use current liabilities only** — A five-year loan is not a bill the quick ratio is meant to cover.
3. **Compare 1.5 with 2** — The sample’s gap is the stock. If your gap is most of the assets, the business is a warehouse.

### Guide

#### The acid test ignores the warehouse

The quick ratio asks whether short-term bills could be met without selling inventory. On the sample, ₹50 of a ₹200 asset pile is stock, so only ₹150 is treated as quick, and the ratio is 1.5 rather than 2. Receivables that will not be collected still count, because you did not tell the page they are doubtful.

### FAQ

1.5. Quick assets are 150.

**How is that different from the current ratio?**
The current ratio keeps the stock and would be 2 on these numbers.

**What if inventory is zero?**
The quick ratio equals the current ratio. There was nothing to remove.

**Can stock exceed current assets?**
The page rejects that. It usually means the two figures are not from the same total.

Divide total debt by shareholders’ equity. 150 of debt and 100 of equity is a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.5. The maths stays on your device.

- Short-term and long-term debt are **one box**. Split them before you type if you only want borrowings.

Debt ÷ equity is the classic leverage multiple. 1.5 means the borrowed pile is one and a half times the owners’ book stake. The ratio divides by equity. Zero owners’ equity is a different situation from a high multiple.

## Inventory Turnover Calculator

URL: https://justtools.info/calculators/inventory-turnover-calculator/
Category: Calculators
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-23

Inventory Turnover Calculator on Toolspire: Divide cost of goods sold by average inventory, then turn that turnover into days on hand using a 365-day year.

### At a glance

- Inventory Turnover Calculator on Toolspire: turnover = **COGS ÷ average inventory**.
- **500 ÷ 100 = 5** turns. Days on hand = **365 ÷ 5 = 73**.
- Use **cost**, not selling price, for both boxes. Retail sales against cost of stock mixes two units.
- A 365-day year is the divisor. A 360-day bank year is not used.

### Features

- **Turns and days together**: The headline is the turnover count. The detail is how many days that count represents.
- **Average stock is your job**: Opening plus closing, divided by two, is the usual average. The page will not halve a single snapshot unless you already did.
- **COGS only**: The label says cost of goods sold so a revenue figure is a known mistake, not a hidden option.

### How to use the Inventory Turnover Calculator

1. **Match the period** — A year of COGS needs a year-average stock. A month of COGS against a year of stock looks wonderfully fast and is wrong.
2. **Stay at cost** — If the stock ledger is at cost, the sales line you want is cost of goods, not invoices.
3. **Read 73 as the sample’s days** — Five turns in a 365-day year is 73 days, not 73 turns.

### Guide

#### Turns are the reciprocal of days

Five times a year means the average stock is sold, at cost, every 365/5 days. That is 73 days. A seasonal business can show a healthy annual turn and still be buried in stock in one quarter, because the average hides the peak. The page uses the two numbers you type and a 365-day year.

### FAQ

**Where does Inventory Turnover Calculator run?**
Inventory Turnover Calculator runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**What is turnover when COGS is 500 and stock is 100?**
5 turns, or 73 days of inventory.

**Why not divide sales by stock?**
Sales include margin. Turnover at retail is a different, usually larger, number. This page is the cost version.

**What is average inventory?**
Often (opening stock + closing stock) ÷ 2. Type that average, not both ends.

**Why 365 days?**
So days = 365 ÷ turns. A 360-day convention would make the sample 72 days.

#### Collection time from one fraction

If receivables are a tenth of the year’s credit sales, customers are taking about a tenth of a year to pay. A tenth of 365 is 36.5. The formula assumes sales arrive evenly and that the receivable balance is typical. A big December invoice will stretch a 31 December snapshot. The page does not smooth that.

**What is DSO for receivables of 100 and credit sales of 1,000?**
36.5 days.

**What sales number should I use?**
Credit sales for the same year as the 365-day count. Leave cash sales out.

**Is a lower DSO always better?**
It means faster collection on these numbers. A lower figure caused by refusing credit entirely is a commercial choice, not a formula win.

**Why can I not type a 30-day month?**
The day count is fixed at 365 so the sample stays exact. Annualise a short period before you type it.

Payment Gateway Fee Calculator on Toolspire: Add a percent fee and a fixed fee on a payment, and show what remains after that gateway charge.

A gateway fee is a merchant charge: a percent of the ticket plus, often, a flat amount. On ₹1,000, 2% is ₹20 and a ₹3 flat makes ₹23, leaving ₹977. GST on that fee, if the invoice adds it, is a second sum. This page will not invent it. It also will not pick a rate by payment method.

### FAQ

## Freelancer Rate Calculator

URL: https://justtools.info/calculators/freelancer-rate-calculator/
Category: Calculators
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-23

Freelancer Rate Calculator on Toolspire: Gross up a desired annual take-home across billable hours and a tax percent.

### At a glance

- Freelancer Rate Calculator on Toolspire: hourly charge = **desired take-home ÷ hours ÷ (1 − tax%)**.
- **₹1,20,000 ÷ 1,000 hours at 0% tax = ₹120** an hour.
- At **20%**, the charge is **₹150**, because one fifth of the invoice does not reach you.
- Tax of **100% or more** is rejected. Nothing would be left to gross up.

### Features

- **The hours are billable hours**: A 2,000-hour year that includes unpaid admin will underprice the work. Leave non-billable time out of the count.
- **Tax gross-up**: The percent comes off the invoice. The formula divides by what remains, it does not subtract the percent from the rate.
- **Zero tax is the identity**: With no leakage, the rate is just the annual goal divided by the hours.

### How to use the Freelancer Rate Calculator

1. **Type what you want to keep, not what you want to invoice** — The gross-up adds the tax on top.
2. **Count hours you can actually bill** — Leave out leave, pitching and bookkeeping, or include their cost in the annual goal instead.
3. **Check 150 against 120** — At 20%, 150 an hour for 1,000 hours invoices ₹1,50,000, and 80% of that is the ₹1,20,000 you wanted.

### Guide

#### Dividing by what you keep

If a fifth of every invoice goes to tax or platform charges, you must invoice ₹150 to keep ₹120. The algebra is desired ÷ hours ÷ (1 − rate). It assumes the percent is a flat share of the invoice. Slabs, GST input credit and a retainer that is not hourly are outside it.

### FAQ

**Where does Freelancer Rate Calculator run?**
Freelancer Rate Calculator runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**What hourly rate keeps ₹1,20,000 over 1,000 hours with no tax?**
₹120.

**What if 20% of the invoice disappears?**
₹150 an hour. Eighty percent of 150 is 120.

**Should GST be in the percent?**
Only the part you do not get back. GST you collect and remit, with matching input credit, is not income and not a cost in this sketch.

**What about unpaid leave?**
Do not put those hours in the billable box. Fewer hours raise the rate, which is what unpaid time should do.

## ROAS Calculator

URL: https://justtools.info/calculators/roas-calculator/
Category: Calculators
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-23

Divide revenue attributed to ads by ad spend. A ROAS of 5 means ₹5 of revenue for each ₹1 of spend. The maths stays on your device.

### At a glance

- ROAS Calculator on Toolspire: ROAS = **revenue ÷ ad spend**.
- **5,000 ÷ 1,000 = 5**. That is ₹5 back in revenue per ₹1 spent, not ₹5 of profit.
- Spend of **zero** is rejected. A free post has no ROAS.
- A ROAS of **1** means revenue matched spend and the goods still cost something.

### Features

- **Revenue, not margin**: The numerator is the sales you attribute to the ads. Cost of goods stays out.
- **A multiple, not a percent**: 5 means five times. It is not 5%.
- **One campaign’s numbers**: Blending two campaigns in your head before you type hides which one paid.

### How to use the ROAS Calculator

1. **Attribute revenue the way your report does** — Last click and assisted conversions will not match. Pick one and stay with it.
2. **Use spend for the same window** — A week of sales against a month of spend punishes the campaign.
3. **Do not call 5 a profit** — Open the profit-margin page if you need what remains after the product cost.

### Guide

#### Five times revenue is not five times profit

Return on ad spend divides attributed revenue by the media cost. ₹5,000 from ₹1,000 is 5. If the goods cost ₹4,000, the ads did not produce ₹4,000 of profit. They produced ₹5,000 of sales that still have to pay for the goods, the shipping and the people. The page stops at the multiple.

### FAQ

**Where does ROAS Calculator run?**
ROAS Calculator runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**What is ROAS for ₹5,000 revenue and ₹1,000 spend?**
5.

**Is ROAS a percentage?**
Not here. 5 means 5 rupees of revenue per rupee of spend. Some reports print 500% for the same fact.

**Does it include cost of goods?**
No. That exclusion is why a high ROAS can still lose money.

**What about a spend of zero?**
The page rejects it. Division by zero is not an infinite return.

## CTR Calculator

URL: https://justtools.info/calculators/ctr-calculator/
Category: Calculators
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-23

Divide clicks by impressions and multiply by 100. Fifty clicks on 1,000 impressions is a 5% click-through rate. Open CTR Calculator on Toolspire.

### At a glance

- CTR Calculator on Toolspire: CTR = **clicks ÷ impressions × 100**.
- **50 ÷ 1,000 = 5%**.
- Clicks **above impressions** are rejected. A person cannot click a view that was not counted, on a clean report.
- CTR is not the conversion rate. Clicks are the numerator here, not purchases.

### Features

- **Views are impressions**: Use the impression count from the same report as the clicks.
- **A percent with two decimals**: 5 stays 5. A single click on 3,000 views will show the small percent rather than zero.
- **No benchmark**: 5% is the sample arithmetic. It is not an industry target.

### How to use the CTR Calculator

1. **Pair the columns from one export** — Clicks from Google and impressions from a social panel are not a CTR.
2. **Do not paste unique users as impressions** — If one person saw the ad four times, the impression count is what the CTR definition uses.
3. **Check that 50 and 1,000 read 5%** — If the page says 0.05%, the boxes are swapped or the percent was applied twice.

### Guide

#### A click is not a customer

Click-through rate asks what share of impressions earned a click. Fifty out of a thousand is 5%. What those fifty people did next is the conversion rate, which divides actions by visits, not clicks by impressions. Mixing the two makes a landing-page problem look like a media problem.

### FAQ

**Where does CTR Calculator run?**
CTR Calculator runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**What is the CTR of 50 clicks on 1,000 impressions?**
5%.

**Can clicks exceed impressions?**
Not in a consistent report. The page rejects that pair.

**Is CTR the same as conversion rate?**
No. CTR stops at the click. Conversion rate starts from the visit or the click and counts a later action.

**Should I use reach or impressions?**
Impressions. Reach is people. CTR’s denominator is times shown.

## CPM Calculator

URL: https://justtools.info/calculators/cpm-calculator/
Category: Calculators
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-23

CPM Calculator on Toolspire: Find cost per mille: ad spend ÷ impressions × 1,000. ₹200 for 10,000 impressions is a ₹20 CPM. The maths stays on your device.

### At a glance

- CPM Calculator on Toolspire: CPM = **spend ÷ impressions × 1,000**.
- **₹200 ÷ 10,000 × 1,000 = ₹20**.
- The 1,000 is the “mille”. Without it you have cost per impression, which is ₹0.02 on this sample.
- Impressions of **zero** are rejected.

### Features

- **Thousands, on purpose**: The formula multiplies by 1,000 so the number is a price people compare in media plans.
- **Spend over views**: Clicks are not in this formula. A CTR page answers that other question.
- **The per-view figure is in the detail**: ₹0.02 per impression is the same sample, written the long way.

### How to use the CPM Calculator

1. **Use the billed spend** — Agency commission that is not in the ad-account number will make the CPM look cheaper than the invoice.
2. **Use impressions, not reach** — A thousand people and a thousand impressions are the same only if each person was shown the ad once.
3. **Check ₹20** — 200 divided by 10,000 is 0.02, times 1,000 is 20. Missing the 1,000 is the usual slip.

### Guide

#### Mille means thousand

Cost per mille is the cost of a thousand impressions. Dividing ₹200 by 10,000 impressions gives ₹0.02 each, and multiplying by 1,000 gives the ₹20 planners quote. It is a price of attention, measured badly, and it says nothing about whether anyone clicked. Compare CPMs only when the impression definition matches.

### FAQ

**Where does CPM Calculator run?**
CPM Calculator runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**What is the CPM of ₹200 and 10,000 impressions?**
₹20.

**Why multiply by 1,000?**
Because the unit is a thousand impressions. The raw cost per view is 1,000 times smaller.

**Does CPM include clicks?**
No. Clicks would make it a cost per click, which is spend ÷ clicks.

**What if I only have reach?**
Do not put reach in the impression box unless each person saw the ad once. The label is impressions.

Twenty-five completed actions out of 500 visits is 5%. The arithmetic is dull on purpose. The hard part is agreeing what a visit is and what finished means. Bots in the visit count dilute the rate. Duplicate orders inflate it. The page will not filter either. It divides.

## Churn Rate Calculator

URL: https://justtools.info/calculators/churn-rate-calculator/

Divide customers lost by customers at the start of the period. Ten lost from 200 is a 5% churn rate. The maths stays on your device.

### At a glance

- Churn Rate Calculator on Toolspire: churn = **lost ÷ opening customers × 100**.
- **10 ÷ 200 = 5%**.
- Lost customers **above the opening count** are rejected.
- New signups do not reduce this rate. They are a separate count. A firm can churn 5% and still grow.

### Features

- **Opening balance is the base**: Ending customers would hide the people who left and were replaced.
- **Logo churn, not revenue churn**: Each customer counts as one. A huge account and a tiny one weigh the same.
- **One period**: Ten lost in a month is a monthly rate. Do not compare it with a yearly 5% without saying so.

### How to use the Churn Rate Calculator

1. **Count who was a customer on day one** — That is the denominator. People who joined on day two are not in it.
2. **Count who left and did not return in the period** — A pause you still call active is not churn until your own rule says it is.
3. **Keep the period in the sentence** — The page prints a percent. You have to remember whether the 200 was a month or a year.

### Guide

#### Replacement customers do not cancel churn

If 200 people started the month and 10 of them left, churn is 5% even if 40 new people arrived. Growth and churn are different sentences. Revenue churn, which weights big accounts, needs revenue in both boxes and is not what this count does. The page treats every customer as one.

### FAQ

**Where does Churn Rate Calculator run?**

5%.

**Do new customers lower the rate?**
Not in this formula. They were not in the opening 200.

**What if I use the ending count as the base?**
You would be answering a different question, and a replaced customer would hide a loss. This page will not do that.

**Is 5% a month the same as 5% a year?**
No. The page does not annualise. Label the period yourself.

## Customer Lifetime Value

URL: https://justtools.info/calculators/customer-lifetime-value/
Category: Calculators
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-23

Customer Lifetime Value on Toolspire. Estimate a simple lifetime value as average revenue per customer divided by the churn rate. ₹50 at 5% churn is ₹1,000.

### At a glance

- Customer Lifetime Value on Toolspire: LTV = **ARPU ÷ (churn ÷ 100)**.
- **₹50 ÷ 0.05 = ₹1,000**.
- The period of the revenue and the period of the churn must **match**. Monthly ARPU needs a monthly churn percent.
- A churn of **0** is rejected. A customer who never leaves has no finite value in this model.

### Features

- **Revenue, not margin**: ₹50 is what they pay, not what you keep after serving them.
- **Same period on both boxes**: The formula does not convert a monthly churn into a yearly one.
- **Zero churn is refused**: Infinite lifetime is not printed as a huge number.

### How to use the Customer Lifetime Value

1. **Pick a period and stick to it** — If churn is 5% a month, ARPU must be one month of revenue, and the ₹1,000 is a stock of monthly revenues.
2. **Use the churn page’s definition** — Opening-balance churn, not a blended rate that netted off new sales.
3. **Subtract acquisition cost yourself** — This page stops at the revenue stock. A ₹1,000 LTV and a ₹1,200 acquisition is a loss the page will not announce.

### Guide

#### A constant hazard, not a cohort

If every period 5% of the remaining customers leave, the expected number of periods is 1 ÷ 0.05 = 20. Twenty periods of ₹50 is ₹1,000. That is the whole model. Real cohorts churn faster in month one and slower later. Discounting those future rupees would shrink the ₹1,000. Neither adjustment is in this figure.

### FAQ

**Where does Customer Lifetime Value run?**
Customer Lifetime Value runs in this tab on Toolspire. What you type or drop in is not sent to us and is not stored on a server.

**What is LTV for ₹50 ARPU and 5% churn?**
₹1,000. Expected periods are 20.

**What if churn is yearly and revenue is monthly?**
The number is nonsense. Put both on the same clock before you type.

**Why is zero churn rejected?**
The expected lifetime would be endless. The page refuses instead of printing infinity.

**Does this include profit margin?**
No. Multiply by your margin after you leave the page if you want a contribution LTV.

## Payback Period Calculator

URL: https://justtools.info/calculators/payback-period-calculator/
